Lab tests on aquaculture and wild fish found RSIV (Red Sea Bream Iridovirus) in 2/2 farmed cá giò from Vũng Áng; one of two also showed Trichodina sp. on gills; VNN, fungi and bacteria not detected in these farmed samples. For wild fish from Thiên Cầm, Vibrio spp. detected in 3/6 cá bơn and 3/5 cá mỏ neo — including V. parahaemolyticus, V. fluvialis, V. alginolyticus; no fungi or parasites reported. Authorities caution results are preliminary; RSIV not yet confirmed as the direct cause. Recommendations include heightened health surveillance, prompt disposal of dead fish, stress reduction, hygiene, and nutrition supplementation; continue monitoring across zones.

triage.headline_ja: ハティン省沿岸海域で魚に病気を引き起こす可能性のあるウイルス・細菌の病原体が複数出現
triage.triage_reason: 魚類の水産養殖・野生魚における病原体検出事案であり、ヒトの公衆衛生への直接的影響は報告されていない。水質は基準値内で、原因究明中の予備的調査結果に留まる。
triage.notes: 本事例は魚類（水産動物）の疾病であり、ヒト感染症イベントではないため対象国リストには該当なし。Vibrio parahaemolyticusはヒトの食中毒原因菌でもあるが、本記事では魚の病原体として検出されたのみでヒト症例の報告はない。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya's first Ebola case: How one traveller crossed borders undetected and what it says about disease surveillance
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease (a form of Ebola) is confirmed in Kenya—the country\'s first imported case. The patient, a Kenyan man who had lived in the Democratic Republic of the Congo for seven years, became ill there and traveled by road via Beni, DRC, into Uganda, then flew to Nairobi on October 3. He was hospitalized on arrival, diagnosed with Bundibugyo virus disease, and died on October 5. Kenya notified the World Health Organization on October 6; as of October 7, no outbreak is declared and only this imported case is reported. Authorities identified 57 contacts, with 10 quarantined, and are tracing flight passengers and other close contacts. Kenya has intensified airport screening, opened an at-risk gate, and begun temporary isolation at major land crossings. There is no approved vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo virus; rapid diagnosis and supportive care are essential, underscoring the importance of border surveillance and regional coordination.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア初のエボラ症例：一人の渡航者が国境を越えて検知を逃れた経緯と疾病サーベイランスへの教訓
triage.triage_reason: 致死性の高いエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス病）の輸入症例が確認され、国境を越えた移動歴があり国際的拡大リスクが高いため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 患者はケニア国籍だがDRCに7年間居住し同地で発症したとされ、感染源はDRCの可能性が高い。確定・死亡したのはケニアだがケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCでの感染状況（既知のアウトブレイクとの関連）について続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Khởi tố vụ án vận chuyển, tiêu thụ lợn nhiễm dịch tả châu Phi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Indictment in the case of transporting and consuming pigs infected with African swine fever.
article.articleSummary: On 8 October 2026, Thái Nguyên's Economic Police announced a criminal indictment for 'Food Safety Violations' under Article 317 in Linh Sơn ward, Thái Nguyên Province, related to transporting pigs with signs of African swine fever (ASF). Earlier, on 17 September 2026, truck 88C-261.93, driven by Nguyễn Quang Trung from Tân Khánh commune, was found carrying many pigs with ASF signs. The vehicle held 26 pigs, weighing about 2.7 tons; the animals were purchased in Hiệp Lực commune and destined for sale to local households and traders, including Đặng Văn Giang in Linh Sơn. At Giang’s facility, 16 pigs, totaling roughly 1.5 tons, tested positive for ASF virus; one pig died. Investigators have charged the implicated individuals and are expanding inquiries to establish responsibility. The case underscores food-safety risks and urges consumers to verify origins and report violations to prevent unsafe meat from circulating.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ豚熱感染豚の運搬・消費事件で起訴
triage.triage_reason: アフリカ豚熱（ASF）感染豚の不正流通に関する刑事事件の報道であり、人への健康被害や新規アウトブレイクの兆候はなく、公衆衛生上の緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: ASFは動物疾病であり人獣共通感染症としてのヒトへの感染リスクは低い。記事は食品安全法違反に関する刑事訴追の内容で、EBSの対象となる公衆衛生イベントではない。発生地域にKhánh Hòa省が含まれるが記事本文の主題はThái Nguyên省・Lạng Sơn関連地域のみ。

article.articleHeadline: 俄罗斯疑爆肺鼠疫　名医提醒染性高死亡率达90%
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia Suspected Pneumonic Plague Outbreak; Renowned Doctor Warns It Is Highly Contagious with a Mortality Rate Reaching 90%.
article.articleSummary: Russia reports a suspected pneumonic plague outbreak in Irkutsk Oblast, Siberia, after a female researcher allegedly broke a vial containing Yersinia pestis; one death is suspected to be due to pneumonic plague. Another employee is reportedly infected with pneumonia of unknown cause. A Hong Kong physician warns plague has bubonic, pneumonic, and septicemic forms; pneumonic plague is highly contagious via droplets and has a short incubation of 1-4 days, with early symptoms like flu but can progress to cough, hemoptysis, and respiratory failure. Pneumonic plague mortality exceeds 90% if not treated within 24 hours with antibiotics. Local authorities have quarantined nearly 200 people to contain spread; isolation measures are in place. Hong Kong’s risk is considered low due to geography and travel patterns; no plague cases in Hong Kong since the 1920s. Travelers returning from Siberia or Inner Mongolia with fever should seek prompt medical advice and disclose travel history.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアで肺ペストの疑いが発生、名医が感染力の高さと致死率90%に達する可能性を警告
triage.triage_reason: シベリア・イルクーツク州の研究所でYersinia pestisの瓶が破損し研究員が感染、死亡例も出ているとされる肺ペスト疑いの事案であり、致死率の高さと人-人感染の可能性からIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域として内モンゴル・香港・中国が付与されているが、記事サマリー上これらは渡航者への注意喚起や香港医師のコメントに過ぎず、実際の発生国はロシア（対象国リスト外）のみである。そのためverified_locationsは空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: Somalia Screens Flyers for Ebola After 1 Death in Kenya
article.articleSummary: Somalia has activated Ebola screening at Mogadishu airport for arrivals from Africa after Kenya confirmed a fatal Ebola case. The Kenyan patient, who fell ill in DRC, traveled to Nairobi via Kampala and died on Oct 5; Kenya is monitoring 55 contacts and has 241 beds set aside in facilities. The outbreak is due to Bundibugyo virus, centered in DRC; CDC counts 8,665 confirmed cases and 4,178 deaths as of Oct 5. Somalia reports no confirmed cases; Puntland says none. WHO recommends screening and contact tracing over travel bans; Somalia has deployed airport health teams and launched awareness. Symptoms include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea and bleeding, with 2–21 day incubation. US CDC notes no U.S. cases; Congo-travelers within 21 days may not fly to the U.S.; Kenya and Somalia are not on the CDC entry list; Somalia remains Do Not Travel Level 4.

triage.headline_ja: ケニアでの1名死亡を受け、ソマリアがエボラ出血熱のスクリーニングを開始
triage.triage_reason: DRC発のエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョウイルス）が国際的に拡大し、ケニアで死亡例が確認され渡航制限措置も取られているため、IHR基準4項目すべてに該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはケニア・ソマリア・米国等が含まれるが、記事の主題である流行の中心地はDRC（コンゴ民主共和国）であり、対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ。ケニア・ソマリアは対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Το μυστήριο της πανώλης στη Σιβηρία: "Κάτι δεν κολλάει σε αυτή την κατάσταση"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The mystery of the plague in Siberia: "Something doesn't add up in this situation."
article.articleSummary: A 28-year-old employee, Daria Sipilova, at Irkutsk’s Institute for Plague Control in Siberia died earlier this month from a mysterious pneumonia, prompting quarantine of the hospital and institute staff. The case centers on Yersinia pestis, the plague bacterium that circulates in rodents and fleas, with bubonic, septicemic, and pneumonic forms—the latter causing rapid, severe pneumonia and potential human-to-human spread. Most experts say the public risk remains low and plague is antibiotic-responsive when treated promptly, though Sipilova’s role at a high-containment lab fuels containment concerns. She was reportedly vaccinated, and Russian authorities say there is no epidemiological risk to Irkutsk. US officials have pressed Moscow for more information; the New York Times notes limited details. Plague continues to cause sporadic cases in Madagascar and the DRC, with reports in the US and Russia, but current risk to Irkutsk is deemed limited.

triage.headline_ja: シベリアのペスト（黒死病）の謎：「この状況には何か辻褄が合わない」
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクのペスト研究所職員が原因不明の肺炎（ペスト疑い）で死亡し、隔離措置がとられるなど異常性・重篤性が高く、IHR基準に2項目該当するため。
triage.notes: 本事例の主たる発生地はロシア・イルクーツク（対象国リスト外）。DRCおよびマダガスカルは散発的ペスト流行の背景情報として言及されているのみで、本記事の主題ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Russland: Was dran ist an den Spekulationen zum Pest-Ausbruch in Russland
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia: What's true about the speculation surrounding the plague outbreak in Russia.
article.articleSummary: Plague in Russia centers on a 28-year-old scientist who died after working at Irkutsk's Pest-Breakment/Institute and near Schelechow; rumors she contracted Yersinia pestis (pneumonic plague), but officials deny a lab accident and cite pneumonia as the cause. About 200 potential contacts have been quarantined; authorities maintain a fast, strict outbreak response, though public trust is low due to historical government denials. The US CDC classifies Yersinia pestis as a Select Agent (Level 1), citing low infectious dose and high mortality, fueling bioterrorism concerns. Historic references include 1346 in Caffa (Crimea), 1720–22 Marseille, and WWII-era Japan in China. Today, plague persists worldwide in rodents with hundreds of cases annually, notably in Madagascar and the Democratic Republic of Congo; in Siberia and western USA wildlife harbor the bacterium, while Germany remains pest-free. Immediate antibiotic treatment is crucial; resistance remains a concern.

triage.headline_ja: ロシア：ロシアでのペスト発生に関する憶測の真相
triage.triage_reason: 発生地はロシア（イルクーツク）であり対象国に該当しない。公式には肺炎が死因とされ、感染症拡大や国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威の確証もない憶測段階の記事。
triage.notes: 記事はロシア・イルクーツクでの科学者の死亡を巡る憶測が主題であり、当局はラボ事故を否定し肺炎を死因としている。コンゴ民主共和国や中国への言及は歴史的・背景的な記述であり、今回の発生地ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: - Mgonjwa wa Kwanza wa Ebola Kenya: Uchunguzi Waangazia Safari Yake Kutoka DRC Hadi Nairobi

The article emphasizes the cross-border travel that brought Ebola to Nairobi and frames the event within ongoing Kenyan health reporting. The piece includes KTN News branding and social handles, such as hashtags #ktnnews, #KTNNewsDigital, #ktnkenya, #KTNTV, #KTNHome and #KenyaNews, along with channel links. The content relies on the title to communicate the key development and highlights the channel’s role in delivering breaking updates on health and related stories in Kenya and Eastern Africa.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア初のエボラ患者：DRCからナイロビへの移動経路を調査

article.articleHeadline: WHO seeks details from Russia on deaths at plague control institute
article.articleSummary: WHO seeks details from Russia on the death of a female scientist at the Institute for the Control of Plague Diseases in Irkutsk. Russia says she died of pneumonia of unknown origin, not pneumonic plague, and denies an institute accident. WHO requests specifics on tests performed on the woman and about 200 others, what materials she worked with, safety precautions in place, and vaccination status. The case occurs amid plague surveillance: just under 4,000 plague cases were reported to WHO from ten countries between 2019 and 2025, with 423 deaths. Separately, WHO warns of a fast-spreading Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, noting an incomplete situational picture and ongoing risk assessment as of 2026-10-08.

triage.headline_ja: WHOがロシアのペスト対策研究所での死亡事例について詳細情報を要請
triage.triage_reason: 記事中でWHOがコンゴ民主共和国における急速に拡大するエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクについて警告しており、状況把握が不完全なままリスク評価が進行中であるため、フルRRAへの移行が妥当と判断した。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシア・イルクーツクのペスト研究所での研究者死亡に関するWHOの照会であり、ロシアは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外した。一方、別途言及されているDRCでの急速拡大エボラ出血熱は対象国に該当し、WHOが不完全な状況把握とリスク評価継続を表明しているため、こちらを主要な評価対象とした。ロシアの事案自体はペスト感染拡大の可能性に関する不確実性が高く、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: ¿Qué visión tiene Mhoni Vidente de la Peste Neumónica? Hubo más de 200 mil personas expuestas según la vidente
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What vision does Mhoni Vidente have of the Pneumonic Plague? There were more than 200,000 people exposed according to the seer.
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague fears emerge in Russia after an alleged Siberian laboratory incident. Seer Mhoni Vidente claimed more than 200,000 people were exposed to a lethal, more aggressive Yersinia pestis variant, with potential spread to Asia including China. No official confirmation of mass exposure or a lab release exists. The case centers on the Siberia Institute of Anti-Plague, where a 28-year-old worker reportedly died after exposure and was hospitalized; reports vary, with some accounts noting about 200 employees were monitored for three days. The World Health Organization has requested information to clarify circumstances and exposure risk. Current authorities report no confirmed infections among contacts and deem the risk of wider international spread to be very low. Pneumonic plague causes sudden fever, severe headache, weakness, a persistent cough (often with blood), chest pain, and breathing difficulties. The claimed 200,000-exposed figure remains unverified.

triage.headline_ja: ムオニ・ビデンテ（霊能者）が見た肺ペストの予言とは？ 20万人以上が曝露したとされる
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・シベリアの研究所における肺ペスト曝露事例が報じられているが、情報源が霊能者の予言に基づく低信頼度の記事であり、公式な感染拡大の確認はなく、当局はリスクを低いと評価している。WHOが情報提供を要請している段階であり、続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事は霊能者（Mhoni Vidente）の予言を中心に構成された低信頼度のタブロイド記事であり、具体的な感染拡大の公式確認はない。発生国とされるロシアは対象国リストに含まれず、中国への拡大も未確認の推測に過ぎないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。WHOが情報確認を要請している点のみ公式動向として注目に値する。

article.articleHeadline: Rusia desmiente informaciones sobre segundo caso de peste en Siberia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia denies reports of a second plague case in Siberia.
article.articleSummary: Russia’s Rospotrebnadzor denied reports of a second pneumonic plague case in Irkutsk, Siberia, after Daria Shipílova, 28, died from pneumonia of unknown etiology. Officials say only two COVID-19 and two rhinovirus infections have been detected among contacts. Initial media claimed the first patient contracted Yersinia pestis in Thailand, but Thai health authorities said they are in contact with the WHO and did not confirm travel. Investigations found no laboratory accident and upheld all protocols; authorities stressed the patient was vaccinated and had strong immunity. The Irkutsk epidemiological situation is described as calm, with over 90% of contact tests completed and almost 5,000 tests yielding no dangerous pathogens. The WHO urged transparent information sharing under IHR; the US and neighbors such as China and Mongolia have sought details on the potential threat.

triage.headline_ja: ロシア、シベリアでの2例目ペスト感染報道を否定
triage.triage_reason: 事例はロシア・イルクーツクで発生しており、対象国リストに該当する国での発生は確認されていない。タイでの感染説もタイ当局・ロシア当局双方が否定している。
triage.notes: 発生地域はロシア（イルクーツク）。タイ・中国・モンゴル・米国は情報照会や報道の文脈で言及されているのみで、実際の発生国ではない。対象国リストに該当する発生国なし。

article.articleHeadline: 俄罗斯鼠疫为何全球震惊？就是数百年前致死2500万人的欧洲黑死病！_手机网易网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Why has Russia's plague shocked the world? It's the European Black Death that killed 25 million people centuries ago!
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague in Irkutsk Oblast, Russia, triggered by a 28-year-old anti-plague institute lab worker who died after exposure to live Yersinia pestis; about 200 close contacts isolated, hospitals closed, and factory staff required to wear masks. World Health Organization and plague researchers say the outbreak risk is extremely low. Plague, historically Black Death, is caused by Yersinia pestis and has three forms: bubonic, pneumonic (human-to-human via droplets), and septicemic; the current case is suspected pneumonic plague, which can be fatal within 18–24 hours if untreated. Effective antibiotics, including ciprofloxacin (about 90% cure for bubonic; 4% mortality), must be started within 24 hours for pneumonic/septicemic forms. Russia’s endemic regions administer a live EV plague vaccine; annual global cases are 1000–2000, concentrated in Madagascar and DRC. WHO assesses Irkutsk region medium-low risk; Europe extremely low risk. Lessons: lab safety, transparency, and persistent natural foci require ongoing vigilance.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアのペストはなぜ世界を震撼させたのか？数百年前に2500万人を死に至らしめた欧州の黒死病だ！
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツク州の抗ペスト研究所職員が生きたペスト菌曝露により死亡し肺ペストが疑われる事例で、異常性が高く重篤（致死的）であるためIHR基準を2つ満たす。ただしWHOは拡大リスクを低いと評価しており国際的拡大は限定的。
triage.notes: 事件の主な発生地はロシア（イルクーツク州）であり、対象国リストに含まれない。記事中でDRCやマダガスカルはペストの流行地域として言及されているが、今回の事例の発生地ではないため verified_locations には含めない。WHOはイルクーツク地域を中〜低リスク、欧州を極めて低リスクと評価している。

article.articleHeadline: Про "чуму" в Иркутске
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: About the 'plague' in Irkutsk.
article.articleSummary: Claims of a plague outbreak in Irkutsk are unfounded; there is no ongoing plague. A young lab technician who worked at an anti-plague research institute died; the institute denies any incidents with plague samples, while bloggers allege concealment. Globally, plague persists with hundreds of cases annually and extended natural foci in Russia (Altai, Tuva, Caucasus), Mongolia, China, and some post-Soviet republics. Madagascar’s 2017 outbreak infected about 2,400 people and caused 210 deaths (roughly 9%). Modern measures limit spread; outbreaks are quickly detected, patients isolated, and treated. Historical notes recall WWII-era Unit 731 attempts to cause plague epidemics by dropping plague bombs on Chinese cities, yielding about 700 deaths over four years. Enemies overestimate risk; the plague’s golden age is past, now posing greater threat to ground squirrels and camels than to humans.

triage.headline_ja: イルクーツクの『ペスト』について
triage.triage_reason: 記事はイルクーツクでのペスト流行の噂を否定する内容であり、実際の感染症アウトブレイクは確認されていない。対象国での具体的な発生事例もない。
triage.notes: 記事はロシア・イルクーツクでのペスト流行の噂（研究所職員の死亡を発端とする憶測）を研究所が否定する内容。実際の症例報告はなく、中国やモンゴルの言及は自然疫源地の一般的背景説明に過ぎず、対象国リストに該当する実際の発生国はない。

article.articleHeadline: Rusia desmiente un segundo caso de peste neumónica en Siberia - Diario de Santiago. Noticias de Santiago de Compostela y Galicia.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia Denies a Second Case of Pneumonic Plague in Siberia - Santiago Daily. News from Santiago de Compostela and Galicia.
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague rumors denied in Irkutsk as Russia’s Rospotrebnadzor confirms no second case after the death of 28-year-old Daria Shipílova from pneumonia of unknown etiology. No Yersinia pestis infection detected; among close contacts only two COVID-19 and two rhinovirus infections identified. Travel to Thailand and a laboratory accident remain unconfirmed; lab safety protocols were followed, and Shipílova was vaccinated with strong immunity. Irkutsk’s epidemiological situation is described as calm with no epidemic risk. Approximately 5,000 tests of contacts have been completed (over 90%), with no dangerous pathogen found, and results have been shared with the WHO. The WHO calls for rapid, complete, and transparent information exchange under the International Health Regulations. The United States, China, and Mongolia have expressed interest as investigations continue; Russia maintains no second case and ongoing inquiries are underway.

triage.headline_ja: ロシア、シベリアでの肺ペスト第2症例を否定
triage.triage_reason: 肺ペストの疑いは否定されたが、原因不明肺炎による死亡例があり国際的関心（WHO、米中モンゴル）も示されているため、続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: West Nile, un farmaco contro i funghi frena il virus nei test di laboratorio
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: West Nile virus, an antifungal drug inhibits the virus in laboratory tests
article.articleSummary: West Nile virus infection could potentially be targeted by the antifungal drug miconazole, identified by researchers at Naval Medical University (Shanghai) as a candidate to cross the blood-brain barrier. In vitro screens showed miconazole reduced West Nile replication by impairing viral RNA production, not entry or fusion. In a mouse model of CNS infection, five days of treatment starting at infection reduced brain viral load and improved survival, with less weight loss and quicker recovery. The proposed mechanism involves host protein TXNL1 (thioredoxin-like 1): miconazole lowered TXNL1 expression; silencing TXNL1 decreased replication, while increasing TXNL1 amplified infection, suggesting TXNL1 supports viral replication. The drug’s effectiveness against other flaviviruses was also noted in cells. The study, published July 21, 2026 in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, used direct brain inoculation, not mosquito transmission; no clinical data, and pharmacokinetics/neurotoxicity need evaluation before trials. Preventive measures against mosquitoes remain essential.

triage.headline_ja: ウエストナイル熱、抗真菌薬が実験室試験でウイルスを抑制
triage.triage_reason: これは実験室・動物モデルでの基礎研究に関する報道であり、実際の感染症発生事例ではないため、公衆衛生上の緊急性や社会的関心の高まりは認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は中国上海の研究機関による抗真菌薬ミコナゾールのウエストナイルウイルスに対する実験室・マウスモデルでの効果に関する基礎研究報告であり、実際の感染発生事例ではないため対象国の発生イベントとしては扱わない。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya ta musanta rahotannin da ke cewar an samu ɓarkewar cutar Ebola a ƙasar
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya denies reports that an Ebola outbreak has occurred in the country.
article.articleSummary: Kenya confirms the death of the first person in the country carrying the Ebola virus, while denying reports of an Ebola outbreak. Authorities say the observed event is the entry of an infected individual into Kenya, with a long travel route from Muri to Kinsangani to Beni to Kinshasa to Kampala, then Nairobi, where the patient was taken to the city's main hospital. The statement frames this as an imported case rather than local transmission, with no additional confirmed cases reported in Kenya. The journey highlights cross-border movement as the infection source chain, and Nairobi hospital care is noted. Kenyan authorities have not announced symptoms or incubation details.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア政府、国内でエボラ出血熱の発生があったとの報道を否定
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス感染による死亡例が確認され、感染者はDRC（キサンガニ、ベニ、キンシャサ）からウガンダ経由でケニアに入国しており、国境を越えた感染拡大の可能性がある重大事案。
triage.notes: 死亡は輸入症例としてケニアで発生したが、感染者の移動経路（ムリ→キサンガニ→ベニ→キンシャサ→カンパラ→ナイロビ）からDRC国内での感染曝露が示唆される。ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCでのエボラ発生状況の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Šta je plućna kuga koja se pojavila u Rusiji i koji su simptomi?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What is the pneumonic plague that has appeared in Russia, and what are its symptoms?
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague has appeared in Russia, linked to the death of a young laboratory technician at Irkutsk's Institute of Plague. The WHO notes pneumonic plague is the most virulent form of Yersinia pestis infection, with incubation as short as 24 hours. It spreads via respiratory droplets and can be fatal if not diagnosed and treated promptly; survival improves when treatment starts within a day of symptoms. Principal symptoms are severe respiratory distress and coughing, often with blood-tinged sputum. The plague exists in three forms: bubonic (lymph nodes) and septicemic (blood) in addition to pneumonic. Global cases total about 1,000–3,000 annually, with bubonic most common in Central Africa, but cases have occurred in Russia, India, and China. Transmission routes include flea bites, contact with infected fluids or contaminated material, and airborne spread from pneumonic patients. Epidemiologist Zoran Radovanović notes the Darja case implies lung involvement and raises airborne transmission concerns.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアで発生した肺ペストとは何か、その症状は？
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクのペスト研究所で検査技師が肺ペストで死亡し、飛沫感染（空気感染）の懸念が専門家から指摘されており、IHR基準（重大な公衆衛生影響・異常性）に複数該当するためフルRRAへの移行を推奨する。
triage.notes: 本事例はロシア（イルクーツク市、研究所関連の検査技師死亡）で発生しており、対象国リストには含まれない。記事中のインド・中国・中央アフリカへの言及はペストの世界的発生状況に関する一般的背景説明であり、本イベントの発生地ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Bộ Y tế thông tin về ca tử vong do viêm phổi chưa rõ nguyên nhân tại Nga
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health reports death from pneumonia of unknown etiology in Russia.
article.articleSummary: Death of a laboratory worker in Irkutsk, Russia, from pneumonia of unknown etiology on Oct 2, 2026, triggers international risk assessment. Vietnam's Ministry of Health, through the Preventive Medicine Department, has coordinated with WHO to verify the event. As of Oct 7, 2026, WHO is actively monitoring with Russian authorities; no recent plague cases have been reported in Irkutsk Oblast. The deceased was connected to the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute; epidemiological investigation and preventive measures, including contact tracing and health surveillance, have been completed, with no high-risk pathogen identified among contacts. WHO continues to assess potential international health impact and verify media reports. Vietnamese authorities urge calm, rely on official health updates, promote hygiene and rodent/flea control, and advise seeking medical care for fever, sudden lymph node swelling, cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath after exposure; avoid unverified information.

triage.headline_ja: 保健省、ロシアでの原因不明肺炎による死亡事例について情報提供
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクの抗ペスト研究所関連の研究者が原因不明肺炎で死亡し、WHOが国際的リスク評価を実施中という異常性の高い事象であり、社会的・政府的関心も高いためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 発生国はロシア（対象国リスト外）。ベトナムは情報提供・モニタリングを行っているのみで発生国ではないため、verified_locationsには含めない。抗ペスト研究所との関連性があり、ペストの可能性も含め続報の注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: RDCongo.- El brote de ébola en RDC deja ya más de 4.200 muertos y...
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo - The Ebola outbreak in the DRC has already left more than 4,200 dead and....
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak, declared in May, has reached 8,728 cases and 4,205 deaths, with 63 cases and 27 deaths in the last 24 hours (case fatality rate 48.2%). There are 1,066 hospitalized/isolated and 2,269 recovered; contact tracing is at 82%. The Bundibugyo strain currently lacks a licensed vaccine or approved treatment. This is the deadliest outbreak in DR Congo’s history and could surpass the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak (28,616 cases, 11,325 deaths). Cross-border measures tighten as South Sudan and Somalia bolster prevention after Kenya confirmed its first imported Ebola case linked to the outbreak; the Kenyan patient is a DRC resident who flew from Uganda to Kenya. Uganda had previously reported 2 deaths and 20 cases connected to the RDC outbreak and had declared itself free of the virus on July 28.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴ - コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行で死者がすでに4,200人を超え…
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上最悪規模のエボラ流行（8,728症例、死者4,205人、致死率48.2%）が継続し、ケニアへの越境輸入例も確認されるなど国際的拡大のリスクが現実化しているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ウガンダ・ソマリア・南スーダンなど周辺国への波及や越境対策強化が報告されているが、対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ。Bundibugyo株には承認済みワクチン・治療法がなく、2014-2016年西アフリカ流行を超える可能性が指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: 3,832 Children With Leprosy: Is India on Track for 2027?
article.articleSummary: India recorded 91,783 new leprosy cases from April 2025 to March 2026, including 3,832 children (4.18%). Thirty-seven children had Grade 2 disability at diagnosis, signaling delayed detection. Child cases signal ongoing transmission; interruption of transmission requires five consecutive years without locally acquired child cases. In 2025–26, 148 districts were provisionally identified as having reached this stage (pending field verification). The five states with the most child cases—Maharashtra, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha—together accounted for 2,565 child cases (≈67%). Maharashtra had 810 child cases (4.29% of its new cases); Uttar Pradesh had >11,000 total cases with 1.43% children; Bihar 702 (7.06%). Nine states/UTs reported >5% child share. Leprosy is curable with free government treatment; early detection prevents disability. Globally, about 174,087 new cases annually, with children ~6%; India contributes a large share.

triage.headline_ja: ハンセン病患者の子ども3,832人:インドは2027年目標達成に向かっているか?
triage.triage_reason: ハンセン病は既知の風土病であり、年次統計報告に基づく内容で、突発的な公衆衛生上の脅威や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 本記事はインド国内のハンセン病排除プログラムの進捗に関する統計報告であり、慢性疾患の管理状況を伝えるもの。新規の公衆衛生危機を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: Koffi Olomide's Independence concert in Uganda canceled over Ebola
article.articleSummary: Uganda’s Ministry of Health has deferred Congolese artist Koffi Olomidé’s Independence Day concert in Gulu City, planned for Pearl Hotel, due to Ebola-related risk. Health Minister Dr. Chris Baryomunsi warned that attendees would include people from the Democratic Republic of Congo, including individuals from affected or high-risk areas, potentially entering Uganda via informal routes. The decision highlights cross-border transmission concerns from the DRC in the context of a high-profile event. The article does not report any Ebola case counts or laboratory confirmations. No additional symptoms or outbreak details are provided. By postponing the performance, Ugandan authorities aim to mitigate potential importation of Ebola linked to the event during the Independence Day celebrations.

triage.headline_ja: コフィ・オロミデ氏の独立記念コンサート、エボラ懸念でウガンダにて中止
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ発生を背景に、ウガンダが越境感染リスクを懸念し高プロフィールイベントを中止するという対応をとっており、国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生上の深刻性からIHR基準に複数該当し、社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 記事はウガンダでの予防的対応（コンサート中止）を報じているが、実際のエボラ発生・症例詳細はDRC側の状況に基づくものであり、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外した。具体的な症例数や検査確定情報は記事内に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Skema air minum di Surakarta tekan risiko E. coli dan stunting
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Drinking-water scheme in Surakarta reduces the risk of E. coli and stunting.
article.articleSummary: Drinking-water scheme in Surakarta, Central Java, reduces risk of Escherichia coli contamination and supports stunting reduction in Margorejo, Kelurahan Gilingan. Coca-Cola Foundation Indonesia (CCFI) with PDAM Toyo Wening launched the Master Meter program, piping main water lines directly into homes at a subsidized rate of Rp2,850 per cubic meter. Shallow wells in the area have high Escherichia coli contamination, contributing to child undernutrition and stunting at this locality. Previously, residents relied on public hydrants requiring manual water collection, limiting safe in-home access. Over the past year, about 50 households have gained reliable access to clean water for cooking and daily consumption, bolstering sanitation and health outcomes. Expansion has been slowed by administrative land-ownership issues with PT KAI, but stakeholders urge continued government support and community-managed networks to broaden coverage.

triage.headline_ja: スラカルタの飲料水供給計画がE.coliとスタンティング(発育阻害)のリスクを削減
triage.triage_reason: 特定の感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、上下水道インフラ改善による予防的取り組みに関する記事であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常性は認められない。
triage.notes: 本記事は実際の感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、浅井戸の大腸菌汚染リスクを背景にした水道インフラ整備事業（CSR活動）の紹介記事であるため、対象国リストへの該当があっても感染症シグナルとしては計上しない。

article.articleHeadline: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Safe and dignified burials help prevent the spread of Ebola
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Ituri Province, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, is being contained through safe and dignified burials (SDB) to prevent transmission via bodily fluids, especially after death. Early mistrust and unauthorized funerals led to exhumations and threats to burial teams; a community-centered approach was created with WHO and Standby Partners deploying Paul Benjamin Gbadia to train and mentor local volunteers. In Jina, Djugu Territory, 36 community members joined SDB and decontamination teams, improving dialogue with families. By 27 September 2026, 11,573 alerts were recorded, 10,357 SDBs conducted in Ituri, and 9,433 laboratory samples collected and tested. Twenty SDB teams (10 mobile, 10 community-based) received operational support, PPE, logistics, and mentoring. Community involvement increased acceptance of prevention measures, reduced resistance, and enhanced trust, with the aim of interrupting transmission and building capacity for future outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：安全で尊厳ある埋葬がエボラの感染拡大防止に貢献
triage.triage_reason: 既知のDRCエボラ流行に関する対応状況の継続報道であり、新規の深刻な公衆衛生上の変化は示されていないが、流行は継続中であり経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 本記事はDRCイトゥリ州で継続中のエボラ流行に対する埋葬対策・コミュニティ参加型介入の進捗報告であり、新規発生や感染拡大の急変を報じるものではない。既存のRRA対象アウトブレイクの可能性が高く、既存評価の更新として扱うべき。

article.articleHeadline: Bukidnon's Valencia City logs 73 suspected Hepatitis A cases
article.articleSummary: Valencia City, Bukidnon, is monitoring 73 suspected Hepatitis A cases, with confirmed infections in Barangay Lurugan rising from 6 to 14 and two cases in neighboring Barangay San Carlos. Most affected individuals are students aged 10–19. Hepatitis A spreads through food or water contaminated with the virus, especially in areas with poor sanitation; the precise source is under investigation, with ongoing case surveillance. In response, ambulant food vending in the affected area has been temporarily suspended pending sanitation inspections. The city government is dispatching two clean-water tanks to supply water for sanitation, specifically for school restrooms. City Health Officer Dr. Michael Escalante urged the public to rely on official updates from the Valencia City Government and the CHO as investigations continue.

triage.headline_ja: ブキドノン州バレンシア市、A型肝炎疑い症例73件を記録
triage.triage_reason: 局地的なA型肝炎の集団発生であり、当局が対応中だが国際的拡大の可能性は低く、情報不足のため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 単一都市（バレンシア市）内での局地的なA型肝炎集団発生。地元自治体が衛生対策（給水車配備、食品販売一時停止等）を実施中。感染源調査継続中であり、重症度や死亡者数の情報は不明。

article.articleHeadline: Seis acidentes com morcegos são registrados no Planalto Norte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Six bat-related incidents are recorded in Planalto Norte.
article.articleSummary: Six bat-related incidents have been recorded in Planalto Norte, Mafra, Santa Catarina, Brazil, in recent days (as of 8 October 2026). The Mafra Epidemiological Surveillance Unit states there is no information that the bats involved were rabies-positive. Nevertheless, people should not touch, capture, kill, or handle bats found at home, in yards, or elsewhere. If a bat is encountered, keep children and pets away and isolate the area until authorities arrive; contact Mafra Surveillance at (47) 99173-3158 (phone/WhatsApp). If there is a bite, scratch, or direct contact, immediately wash the area with soap and water and seek prompt medical care; clinicians will assess and provide rabies-prevention measures if needed. Do not manipulate pets that attempt to capture bats; ensure dogs and cats are up to date with rabies vaccination. Bats have important ecological roles; the guidance focuses on prevention and safety to avoid panic.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジル・プラナルト・ノルテ地域でコウモリ関連の事故が6件記録される
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病陽性の確認はなく、予防的注意喚起にとどまるため、IHR・WPRO基準いずれにも明確に該当しない。
triage.notes: コウモリとの接触事故の報告であり、狂犬病陽性の確認情報はない。地域の公衆衛生当局による一般的な予防注意喚起にとどまる。

article.articleHeadline: Científicos de la UMA vinculan el clima global con el riesgo de nuevos brotes de ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Scientists from UMA link global climate to the risk of new Ebola outbreaks.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreaks in Africa may be forecasted by macroclimate patterns. A multinational team led by the University of Málaga linked large-scale climate oscillations to Ebola outbreak timing, analyzing 49 African outbreaks from 1976–2025 against 26 climate indices. The study does not claim causation; major climate fluctuations may alter rainfall and ecological conditions that facilitate spillover from wildlife to humans. The research coincides with the Democratic Republic of Congo's current Ebola epidemic, which, as of 26 September, has over 8,000 confirmed infections and 3,901 deaths (case fatality ~50%). Four indices showed strongest temporal association: Caribbean Sea surface temperature, Indian Ocean Dipole, stratospheric wind quasi-biennial oscillation, and Pacific Decadal Oscillation, with PDO most prominent. The work emphasizes early warning potential of 6–12 months, guiding enhanced surveillance, deforestation context, and wildlife–human contact studies; a future observatory for updated risk predictions is proposed.

triage.headline_ja: マラガ大学の科学者、地球規模の気候とエボラ新規流行リスクの関連を指摘
triage.triage_reason: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国で進行中とされる大規模エボラ流行（確定症例8,000例超、死亡3,901例、致死率約50%）に言及しており、規模・重症度の観点からIHR基準を2つ満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 本記事は気候パターンとエボラ流行の関連を分析する研究報告が主題だが、DRCで進行中とされるエボラ流行（8,000例超、致死率約50%）に言及している。この症例数は過去のDRC国内流行と比較して異例に大きく、一次情報源での事実確認が必要。スペイン（マラガ/アンダルシア）は研究機関の所在地であり疾病発生地ではないため、verified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Appels sur l'actualité - Ebola : comment le cas confirmé a-t-il pu voyager de la RDC au Kenya?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Calls on the News - Ebola: how could the confirmed case have traveled from the DRC to Kenya?
article.articleSummary: Kenya confirms its first imported Ebola virus disease case and the country’s first Ebola-related death. The patient, a Kenyan national who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo, had been ill for about a month. He traveled by road to Kampala, Uganda, despite an official border closure to curb spread, then flew to Nairobi where he tested positive and was placed in isolation. The article questions how he crossed borders and passed health checks while ill and what measures Kenyan authorities will implement to prevent transmission. The case is imported from the DRC to Kenya, with laboratory confirmation in Nairobi. No detailed symptoms are provided beyond the duration of illness, and the infection source remains linked to the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: ニュース特集 - エボラ出血熱：確認された症例はどのようにしてDRCからケニアへ渡ったのか？
triage.triage_reason: DRCで感染したエボラ患者が国境閉鎖措置をかいくぐりウガンダ経由でケニアに越境、ケニア初の輸入例・死亡例となった。国際的拡大・渡航制限の両面でIHR基準に複数該当し、フルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ウガンダは経由・輸入先国であり対象国リストに含まれないため除外。感染源はDRCと特定されるためDRCのみverified_locationsに含めた。国境管理の不備や接触者追跡の状況など続報で確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Health workers call for protection in Ebola response
article.articleSummary: Kenya confirms first imported Ebola case; health authorities urge protection of workers and strengthened preparedness. The patient, a Kenyan who lived in the DRC for seven years, traveled by road to Kampala and flew into Nairobi on Oct 3, then presented with fever, chills, fatigue, muscle pain, sore throat, and bleeding under the skin at injection sites; samples were positive at the National Virology Reference Laboratory and KEMRI; the patient died on the night of Oct 5. The case followed routine port health screening, highlighting that border screening alone cannot prevent spread. The Kenya Medical Association and KUCO call for adequate personal protective equipment, fully functional isolation units, intensified port-of-entry surveillance, risk allowances, medical and life insurance, and 21-day post-exposure monitoring with paid leave. They demand accelerated Ebola training, especially for border counties (Busia, Bungoma) and Nairobi; strengthen referral pathways and public education, and maintain heightened surveillance ongoing since May.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ対応における医療従事者の保護を求める声
triage.triage_reason: ケニアで初の輸入エボラ症例が確認され、患者が死亡。国境を越えた移動歴があり、国際的拡大リスクと渡航制限の可能性が高く、IHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 患者はDRCに7年居住していたが、エボラ発症・死亡自体はケニアで発生。DRCでの新規発生を示す記述はないため、DRCはverified_locationsに含めない。ケニア・ウガンダは対象国リスト外。

article.articleHeadline: Rússia nega relatos de segundo caso de peste na Sibéria
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia denies reports of a second plague case in Siberia.
article.articleSummary: In Irkutsk, Russia, 28-year-old Daria Shipilova died in a hospital from pneumonia of unknown etiology. Russia’s Rospotrebnadzor denied social-media rumors of a second pneumonic plague case in the Siberian region. Since Shipilova’s death, only two COVID-19 and two rhinovirus infections have been detected among her contacts. Media had speculated she contracted Yersinia pestis (plague); Thailand’s disease control said it was in contact with WHO but did not confirm travel. Officials emphasized no laboratory accident occurred and all protocols were followed; the mother defended the lab handling. Shipilova was vaccinated and had strong immunity. The Irkutsk epidemiological situation is described as calm; over 90% of tests on contacts have been completed, with nearly 5,000 tests yielding no pathogenic microorganism. The government has reported findings to the WHO. WHO urged rapid, transparent information exchange under IHR; the US, China, and Mongolia have shown interest in assessing the threat.

triage.headline_ja: ロシア、シベリアでの第二のペスト症例報告を否定
triage.triage_reason: シベリアで原因不明肺炎による死亡例が発生し、ペスト（Yersinia pestis）感染の噂があったため社会的関心が高く、IHR基準（重大性・異常性）を2つ満たすためフルリスク評価の対象とする。
triage.notes: 発生国ロシア（Irkutsk）は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空。タイは『WHOと連絡を取っている』との言及のみで、同国内での症例発生は確認されていないため除外。検査結果は陰性でペストは公式に否定されているが、噂による社会的関心と原因不明死という異常性からピックアップ判定とした。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en RDC deja ya más de 4.200 muertos y 8.700 casos desde mediados de mayo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the DRC has already claimed more than 4,200 lives and 8,700 cases since mid-May.
article.articleSummary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), declared in May, has surpassed 8,700 cases and 4,200 deaths, the deadliest in the DRC’s history and the second deadliest worldwide. The INSP reports 8,728 infections and 4,205 fatalities, with 63 cases and 27 deaths in the last 24 hours, a 48.2% case-fatality rate. There are 1,066 patients hospitalized or in isolation, and 2,269 have recovered; contact tracing stands at 82%. Regional measures have tightened in South Sudan and Somalia. Kenya confirmed its first imported Ebola case linked to the RDC outbreak; a Kenyan resident who arrived by air from Uganda after travel from Congo. Uganda reported 20 cases and two deaths and declared outbreak-free on July 28. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment; projections warn the outbreak could surpass the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases, 11,325 deaths).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、5月中旬以降の死者が4,200人、症例数8,700人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ流行が同国史上最悪・世界で2番目に死者の多い流行となり、致死率約48%、ケニアへの越境輸入症例も確認されるなど国際的拡大リスクが顕在化しているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ウガンダ・ソマリア・南スーダン・アンゴラは発生地域として記載されているが、記事の主題はDRCでの流行であり、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。ケニアは輸入症例の報告先、ウガンダは既に終息宣言済み。Bundibugyo株には承認されたワクチン・治療法がなく、2014-2016年の西アフリカ流行を超える可能性が懸念されている。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : la 17e épidémie d'Ebola à 8 665 cas confirmés, le gouvernement renforce la riposte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: the 17th Ebola outbreak reaches 8,665 confirmed cases; the government steps up the response.
article.articleSummary: DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, continues to burden the country with 8,665 laboratory-confirmed cases, 4,178 deaths and 2,259 recoveries (case fatality 48.2%). In the latest 24 hours, 62 new infections, 30 deaths and 24 recoveries were reported. The outbreak spans seven provinces and 64 health zones, with Ituri as the epicenter (74.8% of total cases) and Nord-Kivu under close surveillance, including four new cases (two deaths) in Alimbongo. Vaccination campaigns are active in Bas-Uélé and have begun in Makiso-Kisangani and Mangobo (Tshopo) to interrupt transmission. Core response pillars include strengthened epidemiological surveillance, daily contact tracing, dignified and safe burials, and expanded Ebola Treatment Center capacity. The government has decentralized the response, deployed mobile laboratories, engaged community leaders to counter misinformation, and mobilized psychosocial and technical support to prevent health-system saturation in the East.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:第17次エボラ流行が確認症例8,665件に到達、政府が対応を強化
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.2%の大規模エボラ流行が7州64保健区に拡大しており、IHR基準の複数該当と重大な公衆衛生インパクトが確認されるため。
triage.notes: 致死率48.2%、8,665症例・4,178死亡という大規模継続流行であり、複数州への拡大と近隣国への越境リスクも懸念される。既に政府・国際支援（ワクチン接種キャンペーン等）が進行中だが、感染拡大が続いているためフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Union Minister Nadda launches JOSH teams to accelerate youth-led TB elimination efforts
article.articleSummary: New Delhi, Oct 8, 2026: Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda launched JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) Teams under TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan at Bharat Mandapam to accelerate youth-led TB elimination. JOSH aims to mobilize young people to promote TB prevention, early diagnosis, timely treatment and stigma reduction, and to foster conversations encouraging testing and care. The initiative strengthens the continuum of care beyond awareness and screening by prioritizing active case finding, early detection and linkage to treatment, especially for vulnerable communities. Nadda cited WHO data showing India's TB incidence down 21% (vs 12% globally) and treatment coverage at 92% (vs 78% globally), while warning against complacency. Technology will aid speed and reach, with portable X-ray machines backed by AI for screening and rapid molecular diagnostics for diagnosis and drug-resistance detection. The effort involves collaboration with the Ministries of Youth Affairs & Sports and Defence and emphasizes community ownership and participation.

triage.headline_ja: ナッダ保健相、青年主導の結核撲滅活動を加速するためJOSHチームを発足

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Was it a biological weapon? ... Trump comments on the death of a female worker at the plague laboratory in Russia - Youm7
article.articleSummary: As of 8 October 2026, President Donald Trump said the death of a 28-year-old female worker at a Siberian plague research institute is not believed to be linked to a biological weapon. The facility studies Yersinia pestis, the plague, and Russia imposed quarantine measures amid sparse public information, triggering questions about transparency. The incident has drawn international attention, with The Washington Post noting that Russia’s response exceeds typical measures for plague-related deaths. Trump told reporters at the White House that authorities will likely clarify the situation soon and that U.S. experts are reviewing all details. He contrasted Russia’s communication with China’s handling of COVID-19. article.articleHeadline: Конго: епидемија еболе ван контроле, већина заражених умире ван болница
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: Ebola epidemic out of control, most infected die outside hospitals.
article.articleSummary: Ebola epidemic in Congo continues to spiral with most infections outside hospitals. As of Oct 8, 2026, there are over 8,500 reported cases, making this the fastest-spreading and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country’s history. New hotspots emerge in North Kivu amid ongoing conflict, now accounting for about 40% of newly confirmed cases, up from 24% at the end of August. The Bundibugyo virus strain has no approved vaccine or treatment; mortality is high, with North Kivu recording a 58% fatality rate and many centers overwhelmed by shortages of health workers and supplies. More than 70% of new infections involve people not in known contact networks; only 23% of contacts have been traced. MSF warns of chaotic on-the-ground response; calls for community-engaged approaches to tracing, safe burials, and isolation. Kenya reported its first Ebola case, a man who had come from Congo and died during treatment.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue High-Risk Period: Before Puja, Dengue's High-Risk Period, Strict Measures by the State Health Department! Learn the New Guideline.
article.articleSummary: Dengue remains the focus as West Bengal health authorities prepare for the Puja season. Following an emergency meeting led by the health minister, the state announced new dengue prevention measures: 1) an SOP for Puja pandals to curb dengue transmission; 2) a metro rail public-awareness campaign to raise dengue vigilance among city residents; 3) in Howrah Municipal Ward 29, where a nursing school has reported several infected students, heightened surveillance and a targeted dengue drive; 4) hospitals are ordered to treat dengue patients strictly according to the health department guidelines. The department also advises heightened scrutiny for fever lasting beyond ten days, to check for co-infections beyond dengue rather than attributing prolonged fever to dengue alone. These steps aim to shield Kolkata and surrounding areas from the impending high-risk dengue period before Durga Puja.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue or Malaria? 7 Signs to Watch When Your Child Has a High Fever
article.articleSummary: Dengue is a virus transmitted mainly by Aedes aegypti; malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by Anopheles. In children, early symptoms overlap: high fever, headache, body aches, nausea/vomiting, fatigue, and abdominal symptoms, particularly during and after the monsoon in India. Fever patterns can help: malaria may show periodic fever with chills/rigors; dengue may present as acute high fever with severe body pain; but a rash can occur in dengue and its absence doesn’t rule it out. Indian pediatric studies note dengue commonly presents with fever, vomiting, rash, headache, myalgia, and abdominal pain; malaria commonly with fever and chills/rigors. A study of 90 Indian children with laboratory-confirmed malaria found fever to be the most common complaint. Because symptoms overlap, laboratory evaluation and clinical assessment are essential. Mosquito protection is important for both day and night.

article.articleHeadline: CS Duale Responds to Travel Concerns Following Ebola Case
article.articleSummary: Ebola case imported into Kenya from the Democratic Republic of Congo; a traveler died in Kenya after contracting Ebola, confirmed Oct 6. Fifty-seven contacts identified, with 10 in quarantine as tracing continues. Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale said the single imported case does not indicate an outbreak and Kenya remains open to travellers, with response guided by verified epidemiological data and public health protocols. The government has intensified surveillance, set up emergency response structures, and designated isolation, treatment and quarantine facilities with a combined capacity of 241 beds. To date, 268 samples have been tested, with results in 6–12 hours. Enhanced screening at JKIA targets arrivals from 10 countries, including the DRC, Uganda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Angola, Zambia, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan and the Central African Republic. Kenya is coordinating with Uganda and the DRC and seeking international cooperation; WHO supports targeted measures while the US and UK issued travel advisories.

article.articleHeadline: Kenya to seek US permission to use Laikipia Ebola isolation facility
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease imported to Kenya; first confirmed case on Oct 6 and first Ebola death in Nairobi. Kenya emphasizes it is an imported incident, not an outbreak; patient’s journey traced from Buri to Kisangani, Beni, Kinshasa, Kampala, Nairobi, then Nairobi Hospital. Laboratory confirmation passed from Nairobi Hospital to the National Virology Laboratory, Kemri, with Africa CDC cross-check; all labs positive and Kenya notified the WHO within 24 hours. Contact tracing covers 57 individuals (up from 55), with 10 under daily symptom monitoring at the National Police Service Hospital; remaining contacts expanding as flights and staff are traced. Airline passengers/crew total 27 to be reached. Five facilities designated for Ebola care: KNH (8 beds), Moi (50), National Police Hospital (49), Portreitz (4), Nairobi Hospital (133; ~45 ICU/HDU). Kenya’s Health CS Aden Duale notes the US-backed Laikipia bio-isolation facility requires court permission to be used; the US has provided about $887 million in health/humanitarian aid to Kenya, including over $10 million for detection and prevention; no patient currently in Laikipia.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Epidemic hotspots are spreading; experts warn: "The response is chaotic".
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo intensifies as North Kivu becomes the new hotspot amid conflict, accounting for about 40% of recently confirmed cases, up from 24% in August. The ongoing epidemic, driven by Bundibugjo virus (ebola) with no approved vaccine or treatment, has surpassed 8,500 cases—the fastest-spreading and deadliest Ebola outbreak in Congo’s history. Since the outbreak was declared in May, contact tracing remains the core challenge, with only about 23% of contacts identified. The North Kivu fatality rate stands at 58%, with spread reaching roughly half of the 34 health zones. Healthcare centers face staff shortages and stockouts; distrust and burial practices hinder reporting and sample collection. MSF warns of a chaotic ground response and urges community-focused measures. Kenya reported its first imported Ebola case: a man who traveled from Congo and died in treatment.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola alert: State House guests screened before Ruto event
article.articleSummary: Kenya confirmed its first imported Ebola case, triggering intensified public health measures. The deceased was a Kenyan who had lived in the DR Congo for seven years and died while receiving treatment at Nairobi Hospital. Authorities identified 28 contacts—including family members and healthcare workers who attended to the patient—and are tracing 23 passengers and four crew members who were aboard the same flight. In Nairobi, heightened vigilance included screening and temperature checks at State House Grounds as President William Ruto presided over a National Industrial Training Authority graduation ceremony, with Director General Patrick Amoth overseeing the process. Amoth had urged Kenyans to avoid large gatherings and minimize handshakes or hugs to curb transmission during the response phase. The State House screening accompanies ongoing contact tracing and surveillance efforts.

article.articleHeadline: RFK Jr's HHS gave $800,000 to research tied to Russian plague lab
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-08, US NIH funding to UIUC totals about $800,000 (2025–2026) for a Siberia-linked study using foxes from a Siberian breeding facility, tied to Russia’s Institute of Cytology and Genetics and the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute. A lab worker, Darya Shipilova, died Oct 2 after a test-tube breakage involving live bacteria; quarantines were implemented across five hospitals amid reports of pneumonic plague. Pneumonic plague—caused by Yersinia pestis and spread via droplets—can be fatal without prompt antibiotics. Plague remains endemic to Siberia; Mongolia reported a July human case in Khovd province, with 17 of 21 provinces at risk. In the United States, about seven plague cases occur annually (primarily in New Mexico and Arizona); globally 1,000–2,000 cases per year, with Africa (DRC, Madagascar) frequently affected. The debate highlights ethics and a 2022 Biden directive on Russian animal testing, with White Coat Waste noting the 2025 and 2026 NIH grants. Border controls are tightening in Mongolia, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan.

article.articleHeadline: Nadda launches JOSH teams with NCC cadets, MY Bharat volunteers for tuberculosis elimination drive
article.articleSummary: Union health minister JP Nadda launched JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) teams under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, comprising National Cadet Corps cadets and MY Bharat volunteers, to scale community-level TB outreach across 55 districts in 11 states. Each JOSH Team includes five MY Bharat Volunteers and five NCC Cadets and is led by a Class-I officer at the Block/Ward level, serving as a frontline interface for the TB elimination programme. The teams will undertake regular outreach to raise awareness of TB symptoms, promote early diagnosis and completion of treatment, counter stigma, and encourage affected families to seek care. The rollout marks the first phase of expanded grassroots work, with digital monitoring support. WHO data show India’s TB incidence down 21% and treatment coverage at 92% (vs 78% global); 67,933 Panchayats across 697 districts are TB Mukt. India aims to eliminate TB ahead of the 2030 global target.

article.articleHeadline: Kelantan warns: Dogs without anti‑rabies vaccination tags may be culled
article.articleSummary: Kelantan's Bachok district warns that dogs lacking anti-rabies vaccination tags or not vaccinated after April may be culled to curb rabies transmission. The Kelantan Anti-rabies Vaccination Order requires vaccination between January and April annually, with vaccinated dogs issued numbered metal identification tags before local council licensing. Dogs without tags or not vaccinated since April face action, including culling. The policy aims to mitigate cross-border rabies risk from neighboring Thailand, as Kelantan borders Thailand and dog movements could cross the border. A rabies-related death in Kubang Pasu, Kedah last month and a Kelantan stray-dog attack on a child earlier this month highlight the danger. Local councils, with the Department of Veterinary Services, conduct stray-dog operations; two of five identified dogs have been culled. In Bachok this year, 21 dogs have been vaccinated and samples from another 20 have been submitted for rabies testing. Owners are urged to vaccinate, license, and confine pets.

article.articleHeadline: Afrique: Epidémies - Et si le continent s'inspirait de la riposte ougandaise à Ebola ?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Africa: Epidemics — What If the Continent Drew Inspiration from Uganda's Response to Ebola?
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in Uganda was declared ended by WHO on August 27, 2026 after >100 days of response, tallying 20 cases and 2 deaths. The achievement contrasts with an ongoing, intensifying Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Uganda’s success credited to the Emergency Medical Team (EMT), created in 2021, with six regional zones and a target of 480 deployable professionals; current EMT strength is 354 and teams can be mobilized within 24 hours. The response reduced case fatality from 11.1% in 2025 to 5.6% in 2026, versus 41–70% previously. Community health workers (Village Health Teams) and rapid detection, isolation, and treatment were pivotal, along with border controls and targeted risk communication. In the DRC, leaders caution that Uganda’s model may not be immediately transferable, citing coordination debates between INRB and INSP and differing humanitarian contexts in Ituri and North Kivu.
