article.articleHeadline: Suinocultura discute regras sanitárias e combate à peste suína clássica com Mapa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Swine farming discusses sanitary regulations and combats classical swine fever with MAPA.
article.articleSummary: On Oct 6, 2026, in Brasília, Brazil, swine-sector representatives ABCS and ABEGS met with MAPA's new Director of the Department of Animal Health, Marcos Vinicius de Santana Leandro Junior, to outline sanitary defense priorities. The first institutional agenda with the new leadership highlighted the sector's role and addressed key sanitary topics, including Rules for Certified Swine Breeder Farms (GRSC) and the Strategic Plan Brazil Free of Classical Swine Fever (CSF). The participants emphasized ongoing, technical dialogue between industry and the Department of Animal Health to monitor sanitary policies and regulatory issues affecting the chain. ABCS President Marcelo Lopes and ABEGS President Alexandre Rosa stressed the importance of high sanitary standards and sustained collaboration with DSA. ABPA joined to reinforce coordinated actions on animal health, food safety, market access, and competitiveness of Brazilian swine production.

triage.headline_ja: 養豚業界、MAPAと衛生規則および豚コレラ対策を協議
triage.triage_reason: 実際の感染症発生事例ではなく、業界団体と政府機関による衛生政策の協議・会議に関する記事であり、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常性は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は豚の疾病である古典的豚コレラ（CSF）の衛生戦略計画に関する業界・政府間の会議報告であり、動物疾病かつヒトへの感染症ではない。また具体的な発生報告ではなく政策協議のため、対象国リストはヒト感染症を想定したものだが動物疾病のため該当なしとした。

article.articleHeadline: Centre unveils JOSH, youth squads for a TB-free India
article.articleSummary: TB elimination takes center stage as India launches JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The program mobilizes youth—NCC cadets, My Bharat volunteers, and officials—to raise TB awareness, prevention and treatment at block and ward levels, debuting in 55 districts across 11 states as a Jan Andolan. Building on momentum from 2026, when 67,933 village panchayats in 697 districts were formally TB-free, JOSH seeks deeper village-level youth participation. A novel AI chatbot avatar 'Khushi' was unveiled to boost real-time information under the Ni-kshay framework. Odisha highlights: 3rd place in Ni-kshay Poshan Abhiyan and Preventive Treatment, 2nd in overall TB Care, plus strong NAT testing, high-risk village mapping, nutritional kit distribution, and X-ray screenings for asymptomatic individuals. Attendees included Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda, Youth Affairs Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Delhi CM Rekha Gupta, with Odisha's Dr Mukesh Mahaling joining virtually.

triage.headline_ja: インド政府、結核根絶に向け青年部隊「JOSH」を発足
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はインド政府の結核対策プログラム（啓発・予防活動）の発足を報じるもので、新規アウトブレイクや異常な公衆衛生事象ではない。
triage.notes: 政府主導の結核撲滅キャンペーンに関する行政・広報的な記事であり、感染症の異常発生を示すものではないため、対象国リストに該当する国があってもイベントとしては該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en Ituri : un appel à l'abstinence à l'automédication lancé (Un médecin ) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Ituri: a call to abstain from self-medication launched (A doctor) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: On 8 October 2026 in Bunia, Ituri, northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, health authorities warn against self-medication during the Ebola virus disease response. Dr. Samson Asamba of Clinique Marie-claire Babenda cautions that medicines are therapeutic tools, not random items, and misuse at home can cause adverse effects, poisonings, and harmful drug interactions, especially for children and the elderly. He notes that improper antibiotic use may drive antimicrobial resistance, complicating future treatment. Symptoms such as weakness, vomiting, and diarrhea can resemble other illnesses, prompting people to self-medicate and delay professional care. Dr. Asamba urges anyone with suspected Ebola signs to quickly seek care at a health facility and follow medical guidance. The message frames rapid health service use and prudent medication use as a collective duty to protect families and the community during the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: イトゥリ州のエボラ出血熱:自己投薬の禁止を呼びかけ(ある医師より) - ACP
triage.triage_reason: DRCイトゥリ州で進行中のエボラ出血熱流行に関する公衆衛生対応の記事であり、エボラはIHR基準・WPRO基準いずれでも高リスク病原体として既にPICKUP相当の既知アウトブレイクである。
triage.notes: 記事自体は新規症例報告ではなく、既存のエボラ流行対応における自己投薬防止の啓発記事。既知の進行中アウトブレイクの一環として引き続きモニタリングが必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Beni: pasteurs et clergés catholiques appelés à jouer leur rôle face à la maladie - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Beni: Pastors and Catholic Clergy Urged to Play Their Part in Confronting the Disease - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola in Beni, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, prompts a religious-led surge in prevention efforts as of 8 October 2026. Pastors and Catholic clergy are urged to weave Ebola awareness into sermons, emphasizing barrier measures, cooperation with response teams, and avoiding contact with the body of the ill or deceased to prevent high-risk exposure or unconfirmed cases. Damien Kambale Vyalemene, chair of the surveillance pillar for the Beni health zone, warns against misinformation and cautions that some individuals may seek prayers while inadvertently spreading infection. The initiative, supported by Norwegian Church Aid and implemented by the Church of Christ in Congo (Nord-Kivu ecclesiastical parish), is part of an integrated Ebola preparedness and response project for North and South Kivu. The surveillance pillar is conducting broad community sensitization, with pastors pledging ongoing involvement in outreach activities.

triage.headline_ja: エベラ熱対策、ベニ:牧師とカトリック聖職者に病気への役割発揮を呼びかけ - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国・北キブ州ベニでのエボラ出血熱に関する宗教指導者を巻き込んだ予防活動が報じられており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 記事は北キブ州ベニでの活動を報じているが、発生地域データには南キブ州も含まれている。国レベルではDRCが主題であることを確認した。具体的な症例数や感染拡大状況は記事内で明示されていないため、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Dominican Republic strengthens health surveillance amid plague concerns in Russia
article.articleSummary: Dominican Republic strengthens epidemiological surveillance at airports, ports and land border crossings in response to a health event under investigation in Russia. As of October 7, there has been no public confirmation that a Russian research institute worker’s death was caused by pneumonic plague. WHO is monitoring the situation and has requested additional information from Russian authorities. Pneumonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, affects the lungs and spreads via respiratory droplets; it is treatable with antibiotics when treated promptly. The Dominican Republic is not an endemic plague country. PAHO notes natural plague foci in the Americas in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, the United States and Peru, but this does not imply active outbreaks. The measures are preventive and routine and do not indicate transmission or a detected case in the Dominican Republic. DR will continue monitoring with national and international systems and urges calm.

triage.headline_ja: ドミニカ共和国、ロシアでのペスト懸念を受け健康監視を強化
triage.triage_reason: ロシアでの肺ペスト疑い死亡例はWHOが調査中で未確定であり、対象国での発生や感染拡大は確認されていないため、続報を注視する段階。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシアでの肺ペスト疑い死亡例とドミニカ共和国の予防的監視強化。ブラジル・ペルー・米国等は米州における自然ペスト病巣地として言及されているのみで、実際の発生地ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。対象国リストに該当する発生国なし。

article.articleHeadline: Nhân viên y tế ở Nga tử vong do viêm phổi: Có đáng lo ngại?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Healthcare workers in Russia die of pneumonia: Is it concerning?
article.articleSummary: On October 2, 2026, a laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute in Irkutsk Province, Russia, died after severe pneumonia of unknown etiology. The World Health Organization is coordinating with Russian authorities to verify details and assess international risk; there are no recent plague cases reported in Irkutsk. An epidemiologic investigation and control measures are underway, with contacts identified for surveillance and testing; no high‑risk pathogen has been found among those exposed, and monitoring is complete. WHO continues to verify information and collect data on potential international health impact. Vietnam’s Ministry of Health advises calm, adherence to official sources, and basic prevention measures, including rodent and flea risk reduction and avoiding contact with sick or dead rodents. Individuals with exposure history or travel to areas with outbreaks who develop fever, lymphadenopathy, cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath should seek medical care; avoid self‑medication with antibiotics. Updates will follow.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアの医療従事者が肺炎で死亡：懸念すべきか？

article.articleHeadline: Θάνατος εργαζόμενης σε εργαστήριο πανώλης στη Σιβηρία: Αδιευκρίνιστες οι συνθήκες
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Death of a laboratory worker at a plague laboratory in Siberia: Circumstances unclear.
article.articleSummary: Death of a laboratory worker at a plague research facility in Irkutsk, Siberia, on October 2, 2026, prompts immediate public health action. Daria Sipilova, 28, a technician at the Siberia and Far East Plague Research Institute, died under unexplained circumstances. About 200 contacts were quarantined; nearly 5,000 diagnostic tests were conducted, with 90% of the quarantined population released as negative for plague. Authorities stated Sipilova was vaccinated, indicating assumed immunity to pathogens studied at the institute. Officials announced no outbreak risk and began relaxing preventive measures. The official cause of death cited is pneumonia of unknown etiology. Unverified online theories circulated—including a lab incident or travel exposures (Thailand, Moldova) or border-area exposure near Mongolia—but health authorities stressed no evidence supports these claims. The incident drew international attention due to the institute’s work on plague research in Russia.

triage.headline_ja: シベリアのペスト研究所で女性技術者が死亡：状況は不明

triage.notes: 事件はロシア（シベリア）で発生しており対象国リストには含まれない。タイ・モルドバ・モンゴルへの言及は未確認のオンライン憶測であり、実際の発生地域ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Nagy a baj Szibériában: a világ már egy lehetséges pestisjárványról beszél
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Big trouble in Siberia: the world is already talking about a possible plague outbreak.
article.articleSummary: In Siberia, a possible plague outbreak has prompted global attention after a 28-year-old worker at the Irkutsk Pestis Research Institute died of suspected pneumonic plague following a lab accident with a broken vial. About 200 people were quarantined. Roszpotrebnadzor says the death was due to unknown-origin pneumonia; local media claimed a lab infection, but this is unconfirmed. The World Health Organization has requested data on the region and stressed the need for full, transparent information for risk assessment. EU health authorities, Mongolia and China are seeking more information; Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged transparency. In the U.S., plague diagnoses run about seven per year on average, including one case in 2025. The article explains Yersinia pestis causes bubonic, septicemic, and pneumonic plague; pneumonic form spreads person-to-person and can be fatal without treatment. Antibiotics work in 10–14 days; resistance has emerged. A Russian vaccine (live EV line NIIEG) exists for lab workers, not mass vaccination.

triage.headline_ja: シベリアで大問題：世界はすでに起こりうるペスト流行について語っている
triage.triage_reason: 肺ペストによる死亡例とラボ内感染疑い、約200人の隔離、WHOやEU・近隣国が情報を求めている状況から、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際的拡大リスク）に該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべきと判断。
triage.notes: 事象の発生地はロシア（イルクーツク州）であり、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空とした。モンゴル・中国・EUは情報提供を求める側であり、発生国ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Nach Pest-Verdacht in Russland: Was Sie wissen müssen
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Suspected plague in Russia: What you need to know.
article.articleSummary: Suspected pneumonic plague in Russia: a lab worker’s death is under investigation, with the WHO seeking answers. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and remains deadly if untreated. Bubonic plague causes painful swollen lymph nodes after flea bites; pneumonic plague results from inhaled droplets and is almost always fatal. Transmission occurs via fleas from rodents, direct contact with infected animals, or consumption of raw or undercooked wild meat; in the USA, at least 15 people have contracted plague from infected house cats since 1977. Globally, up to 3,000 human infections are reported yearly; current hotspots include Madagascar and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Mongolia experiences outbreaks tied to marmot meat, including 2019 Ölgii near Russia. Early antibiotic treatment improves outcomes; delaying treatment beyond 18 hours worsens prognosis. Europe’s last outbreak was Taranto in 1945. Yersinia pestis is considered a high-risk biological agent by the CDC.

article.articleHeadline: Murder Charge for Wellness Spa Director; Plague Threat Hubbub; Night Owls and ADHD
article.articleSummary: Bronx wellness center owner charged with second-degree murder and manslaughter after allegedly injecting air into an IV line during NAD+ therapy. In Canada, a PLoS One study finds nearly 1 in 15 house cats infected with Giardia duodenalis, and about 1 in 5 infected cats could transmit to humans. Congo’s Ebola outbreak persists, with over 70% of new cases arising from contacts beyond known chains. FDA clears the MycoMEIA rapid urine test for invasive aspergillosis, supported by a new case-control study. CDC revives a hepatitis B vaccination study in Guinea-Bissau. A recall warns that Babies’ Magic Tea Baby Sleep Gripe Water contains ethanol, methanol, and isopropanol.

article.articleHeadline: China gives Kenya Sh260m for Ebola, drought response
article.articleSummary: On 8 October 2026, Kenya received a Sh260 million grant from China (about $2 million), split equally: Sh130 million for Ebola preparedness and response, and Sh130 million for drought mitigation. The funding arrives after Kenya confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease on 6 October; the patient, a Kenyan citizen who had lived in the DRC, traveled by road to Kampala and flew to Nairobi on 3 October, was admitted at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport and died on 5 October. National Treasury Principal Secretary Chris Kiptoo received the grant, with Public Health and Professional Standards PS Mary Muthoni in attendance; Chinese Ambassador Guo Haiyan announced. Kenya has intensified entry-point surveillance, traced contacts, and screened over 652,000 travelers with 267 suspected samples tested; nearly 5,000 health workers trained. The WHO has backed the response, noting the preparedness score rose from 66% in May to 82% in July.

article.articleHeadline: Duale: Kenya has trained 4,971 health workers on Ebola preparedness
article.articleSummary: Kenya confirms its first imported Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease case, with Health CS Aden Duale reporting 4,971 health workers trained for Ebola preparedness. The patient, a Kenyan who had lived in the DRC, travelled via Kampala to Nairobi and died on Oct 6, 2026. The government identified 28 contacts and is tracing 23 passengers and 4 crew members from the same flight; five facilities are designated for suspected/confirmed cases: Kenyatta National Hospital, Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital, National Police Service Hospital, Port Reitz Hospital and Nairobi Hospital. Kenya reports 652,584 travellers screened at 15 Points of Entry; 267 samples tested, 1 positive. Surveillance has investigated 263 alerts from 17 counties. Authorities emphasize that the confirmed case is imported and does not reflect a wider outbreak; ongoing screening, contact tracing and hygiene guidance continue.

article.articleHeadline: "Peste pneumônica": o que é a doença e qual é o risco real após morte de pesquisadora na Rússia? - Revista Fórum
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Pneumonic Plague": What is the disease and what is the real risk after the death of a researcher in Russia? - Revista Fórum
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague in Irkutsk, Siberia, Russia, after the death of a 28-year-old researcher on Oct 2, 2026. She worked at an institute studying the disease and died after pneumonia of unknown origin. Initial reports linked plague, but Russian health authorities reported tests found no pathogens related to her work; about 60% of quarantined individuals were released. WHO says the general population risk is low, and authorities report no plague cases in Irkutsk. Pneumonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, is the most severe form and spreads through respiratory droplets; incubation can be under 24 hours. Symptoms include fever, headache, weakness, shortness of breath, chest pain, and a productive cough. Without treatment, death can occur within 18–24 hours, but antibiotics improve prognosis when started promptly. No evidence of a wider outbreak; from 2019–2025, 10 countries reported 3,847 suspected cases and 423 deaths, mainly in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Madagascar.

article.articleSummary: Rabies Vaccination Day (Dia D) will be held in Eldorado, Brazil, on Saturday, October 10, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. The municipal Health Department and Sanitation Surveillance offer free vaccination for dogs and cats to prevent rabies transmission. Vaccinations will take place at seven urban sites: Escola Sebastião de Paula; Escola 13 de Maio; Escola Infantil Devid Fuzaro; Antiga Escola Cerâmica; Unidade de Saúde Manoel Gomes; Unidade de Saúde Ipê; and Núcleo Municipal de Saúde. The campaign aims to increase access to immunization and reduce rabies risk to people and animals. Pet owners are urged to bring their dogs and cats to receive the vaccine during Day D. Rabies remains a deadly disease; vaccination is the primary preventive measure."

article.articleHeadline: Ciuma pneumonică, boala care poate evolua fulgerător. Cum se transmite, ce simptome are și de ce este atât de periculoasă
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pneumonic plague, the disease that can progress at lightning speed. How it is transmitted, what symptoms it has, and why it is so dangerous.
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, is the most aggressive form, affecting the lungs and can progress within 24 hours of infection. The World Health Organization has sought information from Russia after the death of a laboratory worker at a plague-research facility; contacts tested negative for pneumonic plague. Transmission occurs via respiratory droplets from an infected person; the bacterium also persists in animal reservoirs. Symptoms include cough, chest pain, shortness of breath, and sometimes coughing blood. Although pneumonic plague is rarer than bubonic, its rapid progression and potential for human-to-human spread heighten risk. Reservoirs span the Americas, Eurasia, and Africa, with rodents playing a key role; most human cases are bubonic and concentrated in Central Africa, though cases appear in Asia, Russia, and the United States. Surveillance, infection control, and timely antibiotics are essential; research supports diagnostics, vaccines, and resistance monitoring.

article.articleHeadline: Kenya Receives Ksh 259M China Grant to Curb Ebola Virus
article.articleSummary: Kenya received a USD 2 million (Ksh 259 million) grant from China to strengthen Ebola detection and response, handed over to National Treasury on 8 October 2026 by Chinese Ambassador Guo Haiyan. Of the grant, Ksh 129.5 million will support drought mitigation, and the remaining Ksh 129.5 million will bolster preparedness and response to Ebola outbreaks. The move followed Kenya’s report of its first imported Ebola case on 6 October; the patient, a Kenyan man who had lived in the Democratic Republic of Congo, traveled to Nairobi via Uganda, was isolated at Nairobi Hospital and died and was buried. Kenya sought USD 400 million emergency funding from the World Bank’s Rapid Response Option and is mobilising Ksh 70 billion for outbreak containment, with initial Ksh 2.6 billion set aside and a further Ksh 21 billion expected from the United States. Contacts linked to the case have been identified and isolated.

article.articleHeadline: Епидемията от ебола излиза от контрол
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic is out of control.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak is out of control in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, per Africanews citing Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF). MSF reports a sharp rise in cases, representing over 40% of all newly confirmed infections in the country, with the spread described as out of control. The outbreak began in April; by May, the World Health Organization declared the DRC outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. In June, a doctor who returned from Congo in France was diagnosed with Ebola, marking an imported case. The disease is not transmitted via airborne droplets; transmission occurs only through direct contact with an infected person. Since the outbreak started, the DRC has recorded 8,603 Ebola cases and 4,148 deaths.

article.articleHeadline: WHO offers technical support to Russia over suspected plague case in Siberia: 'We need more information'
article.articleSummary: Death of a laboratory worker in Russia's Irkutsk region on Oct 2 raises alarm over suspected pneumonic plague. WHO offered technical support to Russia and asked for more information to assess risk. Russia says no recent plague cases in Irkutsk and about 200 contacts have been quarantined. WHO seeks details on the deceased's lab tests, the progression of illness, the contacts' health status, and clarity on what prompted public health measures, and whether a second worker with pneumonia has been reported. Until full information is available, a full risk assessment is not possible. Russia has attributed death to pneumonia of unknown origin; concerns about laboratory origin and possible drug-resistant strain persist. WHO can deploy experts if requested, but cannot inspect without invitation. The case has drawn regional and international attention, with Thailand, the U.S. and other countries monitoring the situation.

triage.notes: 事象発生国はロシア（イルクーツク州）であり、対象国リストには含まれない。タイ・米国は『監視している』と言及されているのみで、実際の発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めなかった。WHOは詳細情報（検査結果、症状の経過、接触者の健康状態、第二の肺炎症例の有無）を要求しており、現時点ではフルリスク評価は不可能とされている。

article.articleHeadline: Early detection of tuberculosis stressed to get cent per cent cure
article.articleSummary: TB in India: district-level push for early detection to achieve 100% cure. District Collector Anand Mohan honored heads of 19 tuberculosis-free village panchayats, framing TB control as a social movement with public participation, government departments, students, service organisations and voluntary agencies to reach a TB-Free India by 2030. Symptoms prompting screening include continuous cough, evening fever, sputum with blood, chest pain, and night sweats; individuals should undergo sputum testing and other investigations at nearby primary health centres, government hospitals, or government medical college hospitals. Early detection is presented as guaranteeing cent per cent cure. Awareness drives will run in every taluk with NSS volunteers, NCC cadets and My Bharat volunteers, with local bodies urged to participate. Attendees included Deputy Director of Health Services (TB) V.P. Durai and District Health Officer Murali Shankar.

article.articleHeadline: Pemkab Pasaman Barat lakukan tracking TBC terhadap 5.700 orang
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The West Pasaman Regency Government conducts TB contact tracing for 5,700 people
article.articleSummary: West Pasaman Regency, West Sumatra, launched TB contact tracing for 5,700 people across 57 locations, integrated with free health checks (CKG), from August 13 to October 6, 2026. The program will extend TB tracing integrated with CKG to 90 nagari across the district, with direct community health checks providing education and follow-up based on results. Officials urge residents to participate at Puskesmas clinics or during CKG to facilitate prevention.

article.articleHeadline: JOSH team introduced in Thoothukudi to intensify TB awareness and prevention activities
article.articleSummary: JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) team introduced in Thoothukudi district to intensify TB awareness and prevention under the TB-free India campaign. District Collector Vishu Mahajan inaugurated the program, presenting certificates and shields to 75 village panchayats identified as TB-free for FY 2025-2026, with 12 silver and 63 bronze awards. The Central Tuberculosis Division, in collaboration with MY Bharat, is conducting a nationwide community-based survey across 55 districts to assess TB awareness. In Tamil Nadu, Thoothukudi, Tiruchi, Cuddalore, Dharmapuri and Theni have been selected for the initiative, enabling village-level activities with MY Bharat and NCC Students. Public participation is urged for door-to-door TB screening; suspects with cough or fever for two weeks or more, weight loss, night sweats, or other TB symptoms should visit the nearest Primary Health Centre for screening and treatment. Officials across departments were called to coordinate to make Thoothukudi TB-free, and participants previously took the tuberculosis elimination pledge.

triage.headline_ja: トゥートゥクディでTB啓発・予防活動強化のためJOSHチームを導入
triage.triage_reason: 通常のTB撲滅キャンペーン・啓発活動に関する行政広報であり、異常な流行や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: Salmonella Lebih Bahaya dari Diare Biasa, Ini Alasan dan Komplikasinya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Salmonella Is More Dangerous Than Ordinary Diarrhea, Here Are the Reasons and Its Complications.
article.articleSummary: Reported by JawaPos (Indonesia), citing The Ohio State University, Salmonella infection is more dangerous than ordinary diarrhea and can cause fever, abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and possibly bloody diarrhea. The bacterium resides in the intestines of humans and animals and spreads mainly through contaminated food and water, including undercooked poultry, eggs, pork, raw fruits (melons and berries), sprouts, peanut butter, frozen processed foods, and even flour that wasn’t heated. Transmission can occur via hands after touching infected animals or their waste. Most people recover without antibiotics within four to seven days, but dehydration from heavy diarrheal loss requires medical care. Higher-risk groups are the elderly and immunocompromised, who may develop serious complications such as bacteremia, abscesses, arthritis, reactive arthritis, or rare heart-valve infections. Preventive measures include handwashing, cooking foods to 74C/165F, keeping hot foods hot and cold foods cold, sanitizing utensils, and avoiding raw sprouts.

triage.headline_ja: サルモネラ菌は普通の下痢より危険、その理由と合併症とは
triage.triage_reason: 一般的な健康啓発記事であり、特定の発生事例やアウトブレイクの報告ではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事はオハイオ州立大学の情報を引用した一般的なサルモネラ感染症に関する健康教育記事であり、インドネシアや米国での具体的な発生事例を報告するものではない。発生地域フィールドの情報は記事主題と一致しない。

article.articleHeadline: TPHCM: Tay chân miệng tăng gần 48%, sốt xuất huyết vẫn ở mức cao
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ho Chi Minh City: Hand, foot, and mouth disease up nearly 48%, dengue fever remains at a high level.
article.articleSummary: Week 40 (Sept 28–Oct 4) in Ho Chi Minh City shows dengue fever remaining at high levels while hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) surges. The Ho Chi Minh City Department of Health (HCDC) reports 1,505 dengue cases in week 40, down 2.3% from the four-week average, bringing the 2026 cumulative dengue total to 37,369. HFMD rose to 1,673 cases in week 40, up 47.8% from the four-week average, with the year-to-date HFMD total reaching 38,463. High-incidence per 100,000 residents include Con Dao Special Zone, Ngai Giao, and Minh Thanh for dengue; Con Dao Special Zone, Binh Khanh, and Hiep Phuoc for HFMD. The city records over 3,100 combined dengue and HFMD cases in the week. Authorities urge continued preventive measures, early detection, and prompt medical care; doctors warn HFMD can progress rapidly, challenging even seasoned clinicians.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市：手足口病が約48%増加、デング熱も高水準を維持
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・ホーチミン市における季節性のデング熱とHFMDの定例サーベイランス報告。症例数は多いがいずれも既知の風土病であり、重症度・国際的拡大の情報がなく、HFMDの急増のみ継続監視が必要。
triage.notes: デング熱・HFMDともにベトナムで毎年流行する既知の疾患であり、本記事は保健当局による週次サーベイランス報告。HFMDの47.8%増は継続的なモニタリングが望ましいが、重症度や死亡例の記載がなく、現時点でフルRRAへの格上げは不要と判断。

article.articleHeadline: 俄又傳鼠疫死亡案例　醫界憂俄羅斯恐研發「新細菌」？ - 民視新聞網
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Another plague death case reported in Russia; medical community fears Russia may be developing a “new bacterium”?
article.articleSummary: Russia reports a second death from unknown pneumonia, following a first case suspected to be plague-related pneumonia, fueling international concern about a potential outbreak or emergence of a new bacterium. Authorities say over 90% of contacts have been monitored and nearly 5,000 tests conducted, with no dangerous pathogen detected to date. Experts warn the research may involve a novel variant, a plague bacterium, or other virus, possibly involving gain-of-function experiments that could yield something reminiscent of a new coronavirus. About a month earlier, Russia and China conducted a cross-border infectious disease emergency drill in Fuyuan, Heilongjiang, with Sergey Balakhonov, director of the Irkutsk Oblast plague prevention research institute, participating; questions remain whether China had foreknowledge of the outbreak. Virologist Lin Xiaoxu questions whether the drill reflected unaddressed biosecurity risks. Mongolia has implemented border health monitoring and surveillance with Russia.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアで再び鼠疫による死亡例、医学界はロシアが「新細菌」を開発しているのではと懸念
triage.triage_reason: ロシアで原因不明の肺炎による死亡が2例報告され、病原体が特定されていない点が異常かつ深刻であり、IHR基準の2項目（深刻性・異常性）に該当するためフルRRAへの移行を推奨する。
triage.notes: 事件の主体はロシア（イルクーツク州）であり、対象国リストに含まれない。中国は国境を越えた合同演習参加国として言及されているのみで、実際の発生地ではないため verified_locations には含めない。病原体は未特定であり、鼠疫関連との推測や『新細菌』開発説など憶測の要素が強い記事である点に留意が必要。

article.articleHeadline: The disease that once ravaged Europe still exists: could plague return to Spain?
article.articleSummary: Death of a scientist in Irkutsk raises suspicion of pneumonic plague; Russian authorities report no confirmed cases and negative tests among contacts, with the WHO seeking more information. Plague is not currently circulating in Europe or Spain, and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control notes it has been absent for more than 50 years. The bacterium Yersinia pestis persists in animal reservoirs and fleas and can reach humans via infected fleas, contact with tissues, or respiratory transmission in pneumonic plague. European risk remains very low; the EU Health Security Committee discussed the incident on Oct 7 and the ECDC found no evidence of secondary transmission. The WHO says plague is endemic in Africa, Asia, and the Americas, with Madagascar and the Democratic Republic of the Congo accounting for most cases (2019–2025); Madagascar reports annual bubonic outbreaks. In the United States, about seven cases per year are reported. Spain updated its national surveillance protocol in April 2026 to bolster early warning; antibiotics are effective with early treatment.

triage.headline_ja: かつて欧州を席巻した疾病は今も存在する：ペストはスペインに戻ってくるのか？
triage.triage_reason: ロシア（イルクーツク）での科学者の死亡に関する肺ペスト疑いは未確定で、ECDCは二次感染の証拠なしとし欧州でのリスクは非常に低いと評価。対象国での具体的な発生事例ではなく、マダガスカルやDRCは流行地域としての背景説明に留まる。
triage.notes: 記事の主たる事象はロシア（イルクーツク）での未確定の肺ペスト疑い症例とスペイン・欧州における将来的なリスクに関する考察であり、対象国（DRC・マダガスカル等）は過去の流行統計としての言及に留まるため、実際の発生地としては含めない。

article.articleHeadline: ക്ലിഫ് ഹൗസിൽ അഞ്ച് പൊലീസുകാർക്ക് ഡെങ്കിപ്പനി
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Five police officers at Cliff House have dengue fever.
article.articleSummary: Five police officers on duty at Cliff House, the Chief Minister’s official residence in Thiruvananthapuram, have dengue fever confirmed. Kerala’s dengue burden remained substantial this year, with 11,281 cases and 42 deaths reported up to September; 2025 tallies were 10,886 cases and 56 deaths. June was the month with the highest activity, recording 1,802 cases and 15 deaths. The report highlights ongoing dengue transmission across the state and notes Cliff House as a location with confirmed cases among public servants. The data provide a snapshot of the year-to-date trajectory of dengue in Kerala, indicating persistent transmission but without accompanying information on symptoms, laboratory confirmation details, or infection sources.

triage.headline_ja: クリフハウスで警察官5名がデング熱に感染
triage.triage_reason: ケララ州で持続的なデング熱の流行が報告されているが、今回の事例自体は局所的な集団であり、IHR基準の明確な該当は確認できず、情報不足のため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: ケララ州における年間を通じたデング熱の流行状況（2025年までに11,281例、42死亡）が報告されているが、今回の記事自体はクリフハウス（州首相公邸）での警察官5名の感染という局所的事例であり、季節性の流行の一環と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: 俄出现鼠疫病例 相关个股引关注 市场反应强烈
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Plague cases reported in Russia; related stocks attract attention; market reaction strong.
article.articleSummary: In Russia, a worker at the Irkutsk–Siberia and Far East Plague Prevention Research Institute died from an undiagnosed illness; authorities have not confirmed plague, and the WHO has not verified the case. The incident raises attention to plague risk in the region. China maintains strict plague management; it is a Class A infectious disease with a three-tier system and has reported fewer than five cases annually over the past decade, with no large outbreaks. Plague remains a natural focal disease; while rare, it persists in wildlife and can reappear in humans. The causative agent is Yersinia pestis; reservoirs include marmots and jerboas, transmitted via contact with infected animals, flea bites, or inhalation of droplets from pneumonic cases. The WHO notes it can be very serious; bubonic plague has 30–60% fatality if untreated, and pneumonic/septicemic forms are rapidly fatal without treatment. On January 8, Chinese A-shares rallied in response to flu/epidemic stocks.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでペスト症例が報告され、関連銘柄に注目が集まり市場の反応が強まる
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクのペスト予防研究所職員が死亡したが、当局・WHOともにペスト感染を確認しておらず、情報が不確定なため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシア（イルクーツク）での未確定ペスト疑い症例。中国に関する記述はペスト管理制度の比較情報であり、中国国内での発生事例ではないため対象国として含めない。

article.articleHeadline: República Dominicana activa vigilancia sanitaria ante una investigación por peste neumónica en Rusia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Dominican Republic activates health surveillance amid an investigation into pneumonic plague in Russia.
article.articleSummary: Dominican Republic strengthens health surveillance at airports, ports, and border crossings after information circulated about a possible death of a Russian research institute worker linked to pneumonic plague. As of October 7, there is no official confirmation that the Russian case was caused by pneumonic plague, and no cases or transmission detected in the Dominican Republic. The Ministry of Public Health aims to sustain early detection by screening travelers from areas under epidemiological surveillance, enabling timely assessment, reporting, and isolation if needed. Transmission risk focuses on close contact via respiratory droplets; early treatment with antibiotics reduces complications. The WHO is requesting additional information from Russian authorities and monitoring the case. The Pan American Health Organization notes natural plague foci in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, the United States, and Peru, but plague is not endemic in the Dominican Republic. International confirmation will shape future surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアの肺ペスト調査を受け、ドミニカ共和国が衛生監視を強化
triage.triage_reason: 肺ペストという重篤な感染症に関する国際的調査事案であり、WHOが情報収集中かつドミニカ共和国政府が衛生監視を強化するなど社会的・行政的関心が高いため、フルリスク評価への移行を検討すべきシグナルと判断した。ただし対象国（本評価リスト）での発生は確認されていない。
triage.notes: 本件はロシアでの肺ペスト疑い死亡例とドミニカ共和国の対応に関する報道であり、Bluedotが付与した発生地域（米国・ロシア・ペルー・ブラジル・ボリビア・エクアドル・ドミニカ共和国）のうち、記事の主題として実際に発生が疑われているのはロシア、対応強化しているのはドミニカ共和国のみ。ブラジル等は『自然流行地』として言及されているに過ぎず、対象国リストに含まれるブラジルも主題国ではないため verified_locations には含めなかった。ロシア国内での確定診断は未発表であり、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Beni: appel aux parents et enseignants à renforcer la surveillance des enfants malades - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Beni: Appeal to Parents and Teachers to Strengthen the Surveillance of Sick Children - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola in Beni, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, triggers a call for strengthened surveillance of sick children. On October 8, 2026, Dr. Jérémie Muhindo, medical director of Beni General Reference Hospital and head of the care pillar at the Ebola treatment center housed within the facility, urged parents and teachers to heighten vigilance and monitor children for early detection and timely care. He noted that children in kindergarten and primary school are affected, and that among recently recovered patients is a pupil. Surveillance during an outbreak should be a community responsibility, not limited to response teams, with intensified vigilance in streets, neighborhoods, and schools. The community is encouraged to ensure sick children seek evaluation at the nearest health center or hospital for screening, aiming to curb transmission and improve outcomes.

triage.headline_ja: ベニのエボラ出血熱：保護者・教師に対し病児の監視強化を呼びかけ - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国ベニでエボラ出血熱の症例（子供を含む）が継続しており、IHR基準の『深刻な公衆衛生影響』『異常・予想外』の2項目に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は北キブ州ベニでのエボラ治療センターに関連する情報であり、子供の感染例が報告されている。学校・地域社会での監視強化が呼びかけられており、持続的な感染拡大リスクが示唆される。国際的拡大や渡航制限への言及はないため不明とした。

article.articleHeadline: Moartea suspectă a unei cercetătoare din Rusia reaprinde temerile legate de ciumă. Cât de mare este riscul unei epidemii în Europa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Suspected death of a Russian researcher rekindles fears about the plague. How high is the risk of an epidemic in Europe.
article.articleSummary: Irkutsk, Siberia: a researcher’s death from pneumonia of unknown origin triggers scrutiny of a possible pneumonic plague; Russian authorities report no confirmed plague in the region and contacts tested negative. The World Health Organization has requested additional details and offered support. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and persists globally in small-mammal and flea reservoirs; pneumonic plague can spread between people via respiratory droplets, while bubonic plague is typically flea-bite–driven and septicemic involves the bloodstream. Endemic in Africa, Asia, and the Americas; 2019–2025 most human cases occurred in Madagascar and the Democratic Republic of Congo. The United States reports about seven cases annually; Europe has had no sustained local transmission for decades. The European Commission discussed the incident on 7 October; ECDC finds no evidence of secondary cases. Spain updated its national plague surveillance protocol in April 2026 as a precautionary measure. The overall regional risk remains very low.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアの研究者の不審死がペスト懸念を再燃させる。欧州における流行リスクはどの程度か
triage.triage_reason: シベリアで原因不明の肺炎による研究者の死亡が肺ペスト疑いとして注目されているが、ロシア当局・WHO・ECDCとも感染拡大の証拠はないとしており、確定診断も得られていないため続報を注視する段階である。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシア（イルクーツク）での疑い事例であり、対象国リストに該当する国は発生地としては確認できない。DRC・マダガスカルは過去の流行地としての背景説明に過ぎず、本イベントの発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: New Ebola vaccine trials begin in Uganda amid deadly DR Congo outbreak
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues with 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 deaths (case fatality rate 48.2%) and 2,269 recoveries as of Oct 6. No specifically approved vaccine or treatment exists for Bundibugyo. In Uganda, Phase Ib vaccine trials began on Oct 6 for Oxford’s ChAdOx1 BDBV candidate (Phase Ia in Britain in July) and on Oct 7 for Moderna’s candidate (Phase Ia in Canada in August). The DRC has received 70,000 doses of Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus vaccine), not proven effective against Bundibugyo. Under compassionate-use, 7,775 frontline workers were vaccinated as of Oct 7; an additional 848 frontline workers were vaccinated under the BRAVO research protocol, though BRAVO vaccinations have been suspended due to supply shortages. The outbreak remains ongoing.

triage.headline_ja: ウガンダで新たなエボラワクチン治験開始、DRCでは致死的なアウトブレイクが継続
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのBundibugyoエボラウイルス大規模アウトブレイク（致死率48.2%、死者4,205人）が継続中であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響・国際的拡大リスクともに高い。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・英国・カナダはワクチン治験の実施国であり、実際のアウトブレイクはDRCでのみ発生しているため、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。ウガンダはGeoNames IDが対象リスト（203312=DRC）と異なるため除外。

article.articleHeadline: 加纳4个月内报告450例黄热病疑似病例 3例确诊
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ghana reports 450 suspected yellow fever cases in four months, with 3 confirmed.
article.articleSummary: On 8 October 2026, Ghana's Health Minister Kwabena Akando said that from June to September 2026 the country logged at least 450 suspected yellow fever cases, with 3 laboratory-confirmed. The Ministry has intensified surveillance and dispatched a National Rapid Response Team to areas with many suspected cases in the Upper West Region, urging calm and public support for containment. The World Health Organization notes that Ghana experienced a yellow fever outbreak in 2021, when mid-October to late November saw about 200 suspected cases across four regions, with 70 confirmed and 35 deaths. Yellow fever is caused by a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, confined to tropical Africa and the Americas. Symptoms include high fever, headache, jaundice, and bleeding; there is no specific antiviral treatment, but vaccination is effective prevention.

triage.headline_ja: ガーナ、4か月間で黄熱病疑い例450件、うち3件が確定診断
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準のうち『重篤性』『異常性』の2項目に該当し、WPRO基準も複数該当するためフルリスク評価への移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はガーナにおける黄熱病疑い例・確定例の急増であり、Canary Islands・Spain・Africa大陸などの発生地域情報は本イベントの主題ではないため除外した。2021年の過去流行（70例確定、35例死亡）がWHOにより言及されており、重症化リスクの参考情報として記載。

article.articleHeadline: Johan Nilsson: Vad är lungpest - och ska vi oroa oss?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Johan Nilsson: What is pneumonic plague - and should we be worried?
article.articleSummary: As of 8 October 2026, a 28-year-old laboratory technician, Darja Sjipilova, died overnight of 2 October at a hospital outside Irkutsk, Russia; officials initially cited pneumonia of unknown origin, but rapid reporting raised concerns she had contracted pneumonic plague. Russian authorities quarantined the hospital and contacts, while WHO, the United States, and the European Union demanded more information. Pneumonic plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and has three forms: bubonic, septicemic, and pneumonic; only pneumonic plague can spread between people, via droplet transmission during close contact. It progresses rapidly and is nearly always fatal if untreated, though antibiotics are effective when begun within 24 hours of symptoms. No vaccine exists. Preventive antibiotics are used for exposed individuals; Russia maintains extensive plague laboratory networks. The bacterium circulates among rodents in Russia, Mongolia, and China.

triage.headline_ja: ヨハン・ニルソン：肺ペストとは何か、我々は懸念すべきか？
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクで肺ペスト疑いの死亡例が発生し検疫措置が取られWHO等が情報を求めているが、対象国（露・蒙・中）のうち中国は病原体循環地域として言及されるのみで実際の発生国ではなく、続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 発生国ロシア（イルクーツク）は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空。モンゴル・中国は病原体が齧歯類間で循環する地域として言及されているのみで、実際の症例発生地ではない。

article.articleHeadline: W.H.O warns safe burial practices remain critical in Ebola response
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Ituri Province of northeast Democratic Republic of Congo, caused by Bundibugyo virus, remains active. Transmission occurs via contact with infected bodily fluids, including those of deceased individuals, making safe and dignified burials critical to containment. As of September, Ituri recorded more than 11,573 alerts and conducted 10,357 safe and dignified burials. WHO notes that involving community members in burial teams has reduced resistance and improved cooperation with health authorities. Ongoing surveillance, infection prevention, and sustained community engagement are essential to controlling the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、エボラ対応における安全な埋葬慣行の重要性を警告
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州でBundibugyoウイルスによるエボラアウトブレイクが継続中であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響、流行継続の可能性、国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: WHOが安全な埋葬の重要性を強調していることから、アウトブレイクは依然として活発であり、継続的な監視と国際支援が必要と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Η Ρωσία διαψεύδει τις αναφορές για δεύτερο ύποπτο κρούσμα πανώλης
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia denies reports of a second suspected case of plague.
article.articleSummary: As of 8 October 2026, Russia’s Rospotrebnadzor denied social-media reports of a second suspected plague case linked to the death of a 28-year-old researcher at the Irkutsk-based Research Institute for Plague Prevention of Siberia and the Far East. Investigations of the deceased’s contacts concluded without any illness related to an infectious disease, and some 5,000 laboratory tests found no dangerous pathogens. The agency did not confirm whether Daria Sipirova’s death was due to Yersinia pestis, despite pressure from the World Health Organization, the EU, and the United States for an explanation. The WHO noted the publicly reported information, while Russia described pneumonia of unknown cause as the death. Plague is treatable with antibiotics, transmitted by fleas or respiratory droplets, and can have high fatality without treatment. The disease is endemic in Africa, parts of the former Soviet Union, South America, and Asia, with recent cases mainly in DRC and Madagascar.

triage.headline_ja: ロシア、ペスト疑いの2例目報告を否定

article.articleHeadline: Kenya begins contact tracing after COVID-19 patient dies at Nairobi hospital
article.articleSummary: Kenya launches contact tracing after an imported Ebola Bundibugyo strain case caused Kenya’s first Ebola death in Nairobi. The patient was a local man from the Democratic Republic of the Congo who became ill there and arrived in Kenya from Kampala/Entebbe, Uganda on Oct 3, dying at a Nairobi hospital. WHO Kenya Representative Dr. Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo said the coming days are decisive to prevent community spread. Authorities have traced about 10 relatives who volunteered for quarantine and are under observation, plus 21 health workers, lab nurses, and others who treated the patient. No infections detected to date. The response emphasizes completing contact lists and quarantine within a two-to-eight-day monitoring window to contain the outbreak in Kenya.

triage.notes: 患者はDRC出身でDRCで発症、ウガンダ（カンパラ/エンテベ）経由でケニアのナイロビに到着し死亡。ケニア・ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため、感染源であるDRCのみをverified_locationsに記載。見出し原文はエボラではなくCOVID-19と誤表記されているが、記事サマリーはエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）の症例であることを明記している点に注意。

article.articleHeadline: Cette alerte est inquiétante, mais...": y a-t-il un risque de diffusion de la peste en Europe?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "This alert is worrying, but...": Is there a risk of plague spreading in Europe?
article.articleSummary: No risk of plague spreading in Europe is reported by Dr. Anne-Sophie Le Guern, director of the Pasteur Institute’s National Reference Center for Plague, following the death of a Russian laboratory worker studying the disease. Plague is a wild rodent disease transmitted rodent-to-rodent via fleas, caused by Yersinia pestis circulating in animal reservoirs. The largest animal and human foci are in Africa: Madagascar is endemic with 100-500 human cases annually, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 100-300 cases. Additional animal foci exist in wildlife in the Western United States, across South America including Peru and Brazil, with recent detections in Mongolia and China. The article emphasizes Europe’s lack of spread risk while highlighting the broader global distribution of reservoirs and associated human cases tied to these foci.

triage.headline_ja: 「この警告は不安をあおるが...」：ヨーロッパでペストが拡散するリスクはあるのか？

triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシアの研究所従事者の死亡事例とそれに伴うヨーロッパへの拡散リスクの否定であり、対象国（DRC、ブラジル、中国等）はペストの常在地域として背景情報として言及されているのみで、新規の発生イベントではないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Peste, a doença medieval que nunca desapareceu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Plague, the Medieval Disease That Never Disappeared.
article.articleSummary: Plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, persists worldwide in three forms: bubonic (fleas from infected rodents cause painful lymph node swelling), septicemic, and pneumonic (airborne transmission between people). Without treatment, it is almost always fatal. The United States sees occasional West Coast cases; Madagascar reports 250–500 infections annually, with the 2017 outbreak the latest large one. Africa's affected countries include the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. Europe’s Black Death (1347–1353) killed about 25 million, roughly 60% of the population, though the bacterium predates medieval times. After 1945 Europe had no sustained cases; Corsica recorded the last. The pathogen evolved to spread via fleas after acquiring the ymt gene in the Bronze Age, enabling pandemics. A US case in Oregon illustrates diagnostic challenges, with a misdiagnosed patient dying before plague was considered; another patient, Paul Gaylord, survived after later recognition. The Robert Koch Institute and colleagues seek faster laboratory diagnosis to save lives.

triage.headline_ja: ペスト、決して消えなかった中世の病
triage.triage_reason: 特定の現在進行中のアウトブレイクを報じる記事ではなく、ペストの歴史・病理・過去事例を解説する一般教養記事であるため、シグナルとして取り上げる根拠が乏しい。
triage.notes: 記事はペストの歴史・病原体・診断の難しさを扱う解説記事であり、具体的な現在進行中のアウトブレイク報告ではない。DRCは『アフリカの流行国』として言及されているのみで、具体的な発生状況の記述はない。

article.articleHeadline: Charbon bactérien : l'eau de la Semuliki interdite à Kasindi, des spores qui durent des années
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Anthrax: Semuliki River water banned in Kasindi, spores lasting for years.
article.articleSummary: On 6 October 2026, Nord-Kivu authorities banned use of Semuliki River water in Kasindi-Lubirigha, about 90 kilometers from Beni, after hippo carcasses were found along the riverbed and linked to anthrax (Bacillus anthracis). Bacterial spores can survive for years in water and sediments, making the ban effectively long-lasting rather than temporary. Human infection occurs via contact with an infected animal or its products, ingestion, or rarely inhalation. Kambo and Ihunga depend on the river for drinking, cooking, and cleaning, forcing women and girls to walk six to seven kilometers daily to Kasindi for water. No end date for the restriction. Local groups lack resources to extend potable-water networks; calls for funding to expand supply. Nord-Kivu faces Ebola and a cholera burden—3,124 deaths across sixteen provinces—and more than 33,000 malnutrition cases (MSF-supported Jan–Aug). Semuliki forms Uganda border and wildlife corridor, suggesting cross-border veterinary surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: 炭疽菌：カシンディでセムリキ川の水使用禁止、胞子は数年間残存
triage.triage_reason: ノースキブ州でカバ（カバの死骸）由来の炭疽菌汚染によりセムリキ川の水利用が禁止され、国境地帯・野生生物回廊での越境拡大リスクと住民の継続的曝露が懸念されるため、IHR基準2項目（異常性・国際拡大リスク）に該当しフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はDRCノースキブ州カシンディでのカバ死骸由来炭疽菌汚染と飲料水禁止措置。ウガンダは国境・野生生物回廊として言及されるのみで実際の発生地ではなく、ナイジェリアは本文中で言及なしのため除外。背景としてエボラ・コレラ流行（3,124人死亡）にも言及されているが、本記事の中心イベントは炭疽菌汚染である。

article.articleHeadline: DRC records 8,665 Ebola cases, 4,178 deaths as Kenya reports imported case
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-08, the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has 8,665 confirmed cases and 4,178 deaths, with transmission slowing in some areas but growing elsewhere. WHO director-general Tedros Ghebreyesus reported improvements in contact tracing—about 2,000 alerts daily and nearly five million people reached—while clinical trials of Ebola therapeutics exceed 600 participants and a vaccine trial is expected later in October, with equity of access a priority. Nevertheless, most deaths still occur in communities rather than treatment centres, and contact tracing has not reached containment levels amid a prolonged humanitarian crisis and new hotspots, including near the South Sudan border. Kenya reported its first imported Ebola case, a traveler from the DRC via Uganda who died in Nairobi; 55 contacts, including passengers and crew, are being monitored, with WHO supporting Kenya’s response and stressing preparedness over travel bans.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでエボラ出血熱が8,665症例・4,178人死亡、ケニアで輸入症例確認

article.articleHeadline: Centre launches youth-led teams in 55 districts to boost TB elimination drive
article.articleSummary: TB elimination drive in India expanded with 55 districts in 11 states/UTs launching youth-led JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) Teams. Each team includes five MY Bharat volunteers and five NCC cadets, supervised by a Class-I officer at block/ward level. They will raise TB awareness, promote early diagnosis, support treatment completion, and address stigma. First phase covers 55 districts; expansion planned nationwide. The initiative, under TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, aligns with India reporting a 21% decline in TB incidence and 92% treatment coverage, higher than global benchmarks (12% and 78% respectively). 67,933 panchayats across 697 districts recognised as TB Mukt in 2026. Tools launched include a JOSH flipbook, brochure, e-Sangini service Khushi Avatar in 12 languages, and a JOSH Teams feature in the TB Mukt Bharat App to monitor activities.

article.articleHeadline: 49% dos municípios estão em situação de alerta ou risco contra o Aedes aegypti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 49% of municipalities are in a state of alert or at risk from Aedes aegypti.
article.articleSummary: Brazil's Health Ministry released the second-cycle results of the Rapid Indices for Aedes aegypti (LIRAa), covering May–August 2026. Of 3,732 municipalities evaluated, 49.2% are in alert or at risk for Aedes aegypti presence, signaling ongoing transmission risk for dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. The survey identifies key breeding sites: daily containers such as plant pots and plant dishes (42.3%), water-storage reservoirs like tanks and cisterns (26.1%), and tires and solid waste (23%). Regional differences include the North with tires/solid waste, the Northeast with water-storage containers, and the Southeast, South, and Central-West with plant-related containers. El Niño-driven summer conditions heighten risk, guiding prevention actions by Endemic Disease Control Agents and Community Health Agents to identify and treat persistent breeding sites and educate communities. By year-end, 300,000 more professionals will be trained. Public guidance emphasizes regular home inspections to eliminate water-accumulation sites; see Massa.com.br for more information.

article.articleHeadline: Ministério da Saúde emite alerta de risco para presença do mosquito Aedes Aegypti em municípios
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health issues a risk alert for the presence of the Aedes aegypti mosquito in municipalities
article.articleSummary: Brazil's Ministry of Health issued a risk alert on the presence of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in municipalities nationwide. Nearly half of evaluated cities are in alert or at risk for Aedes aegypti, the vector of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. Data collected between May and August 2026 show the main breeding sites are water-holding containers such as plant pots and saucers, bottles, and other receptacles that accumulate standing water, followed by water storage tanks (caixas d'água) and large drums (tonéis). Additional breeding grounds include tires, PET bottles, cans, and improperly discarded waste. The results aim to help Brazilian states and municipalities target vector-control actions and disease prevention efforts, aligning resources to reduce transmission risks associated with the Aedes aegypti vector.

article.articleHeadline: Plague Cases Still Reported in the US: See Where
article.articleSummary: CDC will screen travelers from Siberia for pneumonic plague after a plague laboratory researcher’s death in the far east region; the risk to the United States is extremely low. In the United States, an Arizona man died last year after exposure to plague-infected cats, and a New Mexico woman died earlier this year. Most US cases occur in the western states—northern New Mexico, northern Arizona, southern Colorado, California, southern Oregon, and far western Nevada—with isolated cases in Montana, Michigan, Connecticut, Idaho, Texas, Oklahoma, and Alabama. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and has three forms: bubonic (most common), septicemic, and pneumonic (easily transmitted person-to-person). Buboes are swollen lymph nodes; early antibiotic treatment is curative. Prevention: rodent control and flea protection for pets. Worldwide, Congo, Madagascar, and Peru report most plague; the US averages about five cases per year, most bubonic. Since 2000, the highest total was 17 cases in 2006.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Kenya marks first case and fatality in Bundibugyo strain outbreak
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease has reached Kenya with its first confirmed case and fatality in the ongoing outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The patient, a Kenyan citizen who fell ill in the DRC, traveled overland through Uganda and flew to Nairobi, testing positive for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease. He presented fever, fatigue, chills, and sore throat, and died on 5 October 2026; burial occurred on 6 October 2026 under Kenya’s Ebola safe and dignified burial protocol. Kenya identified 57 contacts linked to the case, including passengers and family members. The World Health Organization warns that a rapid rise in infections and deaths in the DRC, if not contained, could trigger further regional spread to additional countries, underscoring cross-border transmission risks.

article.articleHeadline: Nach Laborvorfall in Sibirien: Faktencheck zu Pest-Mythen
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: After a laboratory incident in Siberia: Fact-check on plague myths.
article.articleSummary: Three plague myths debunked after a Siberian laboratory incident. Myth 1: plague is medieval and eradicated. Actually Yersinia pestis causes about 1,000–3,000 global cases yearly, with the Democratic Republic of Congo and Madagascar as hotspots; the United States reports roughly seven cases annually. Pneumonic plague presents fever, chills, headache, shortness of breath, and sometimes bloody cough, and can kill within 1–2 days if untreated. A London study comparing medieval strains to today’s found no genetic differences, underscoring persistent risk from animal reservoirs worldwide (Australia and the Pacific largely free). Myth 2: plague is ultra-contagious. Transmission requires close contact and droplet spread; pneumonic plague is mainly dangerous within two meters. Myth 3: infection is a death sentence. Antibiotics work when diagnosed and treated quickly; untreated pneumonic plague mortality approaches 100%. Irkutsk incident: a 28-year-old scientist died; about 200 people quarantined; WHO seeking information.

triage.notes: 事件の主な発生地はロシア（イルクーツク）であり対象国リストに含まれない。DRC・マダガスカルへの言及はペストの一般的な流行地としての背景情報であり、本記事の主題イベントの発生地ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: IIT BHU scientists develop novel green light-activated technology to fight bacterial infections
article.articleSummary: Varanasi’s IIT (BHU) researchers report green-light-activated Os(II) metallophotoantibiotics that inhibit bacterial growth, disrupt biofilms, and accelerate infected-wound healing. Published in Communications Chemistry (Nature Portfolio) on 8 October 2026, the work from Dr. Samya Banerjee and Dr. Sudip Mukherjee, with Apurba Mandal and colleagues, describes three Os(II) compounds—Os1, Os2, Os3—that become bactericidal under green light by generating reactive oxygen species. In tests against Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Bacillus subtilis, Os1 was the most promising. Notably, Os1 under green light achieved about 85% inhibition of biofilm formation in E. coli and Bacillus subtilis, addressing biofilm-associated persistence on surfaces and medical devices. In rat models, the compounds accelerated healing of infected wounds, highlighting potential against antimicrobial resistance and persistent infections.

article.articleHeadline: O que é a peste pneumônica, quais os sintomas e por que ela é tão perigosa?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What is pneumonic plague, what are its symptoms, and why is it so dangerous?
article.articleSummary: In Siberia, Russia, a 28-year-old researcher at an institute studying dangerous pathogens died under investigation for pneumonic plague, the most severe form caused by Yersinia pestis. The World Health Organization is monitoring the case, but the cause remains unconfirmed. Pneumonic plague attacks the lungs and can be fatal within 18–24 hours without treatment. Key symptoms include high fever with chills, headache and body aches, cough (potentially bloody), shortness of breath, chest pain, fatigue, nausea and vomiting. Transmission occurs via respiratory droplets between people and can also occur through contact with infected animals, with spread most likely when the patient is symptomatic. Early antibiotic therapy is critical and should begin within about 15 hours of symptom onset, even before lab confirmation. Brazil has had no human plague cases since 2005 (Pedra Branca, Ceará), though the bacterium persists in wild rodents. The WHO regards international spread as low risk.

triage.headline_ja: 肺ペストとは何か、その症状とそれがなぜ危険なのか？

article.articleHeadline: Potrafi zabić w 48 godzin. Ekspert mówi, czy grozi nam epidemia dżumy? - Super Nowości - wiadomości z Rzeszowa i Podkarpacia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: It can kill within 48 hours. An expert says whether we are facing a plague epidemic? - Super Nowości - news from Rzeszów and Podkarpacia.
article.articleSummary: 28-year-old laboratory worker at the Institute for Plague Research in Irkutsk died of pneumonia. Dr. Rajewski says there is no basis for an epidemic; while circumstances may hint at plague, evidence is not conclusive, and Russia reports no further cases or human-to-human transmission. The last confirmed plague case in Russia was 2016; sporadic cases have occurred abroad, including New Mexico, Madagascar, and the DRC. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis, transmitted mainly by flea bites; pneumonic plague can spread via droplets. Incubation is 1–7 days, shorter in pneumonic form. Early symptoms: fever, chills, headache, weakness. Forms: bubonic, septicemic, pneumonic—the latter most dangerous with rapid pneumonia and respiratory failure. Untreated mortality can reach 50%, with death in 24–48 hours for pneumonic/septicemic forms. Antibiotics (aminoglycosides, doxycycline, fluoroquinolones) are effective; vaccines are not widely available. The pathogen is cited as a potential biological weapon. Monitoring and confirmation of the lab worker’s death continue.

article.articleHeadline: Staffel fünf kommt im Dezember: ARD: Neue "Charité"-Staffel behandelt Cholera in Berlin 1831
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Season five premieres in December: ARD: New 'Charité' season deals with cholera in Berlin, 1831.
article.articleSummary: Season five of the ARD series Charité is set in Berlin in 1831 amid a cholera outbreak, with filming around Prague. Streaming starts December 18, and TV broadcast is planned for December 22. The narrative centers on Underarzt Overath, a junior doctor who is secretly a woman, as the arrival of her former fiancé at the Charité intersects with the citywide crisis and the challenge of stopping and treating the disease. Cholera is described as a highly contagious diarrheal illness caused by Vibrio cholerae, transmitted via contaminated drinking water and food. Severe dehydration can kill within hours; rapid fluid and electrolyte replacement is essential. Historically, cholera spread from the Ganges Delta and recurs after disasters or conflicts. Cast includes Marlene Burow, Philip Froissant, Idan Weiss, Jan Krauter, Anna Schudt, Dominic Raacke, Harald Krassnitzer; directed by Alexander Dierbach. The series previously shifted to a 2049 setting before returning to history.

triage.headline_ja: シーズン5は12月に登場:ARD、新『シャリテ』シーズンは1831年ベルリンのコレラを描く
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はテレビドラマ『Charité』シーズン5の制作に関する娯楽記事であり、実際の感染症発生事例ではない。
triage.notes: 1831年のベルリンを舞台にした歴史ドラマの話題であり、現実の公衆衛生イベントではない。発生地域に記載されたインド・バングラデシュ・チェコ・ドイツはいずれもドラマの撮影地・歴史的背景に過ぎず、実際のコレラ発生国ではない。

article.articleHeadline: ARD: Neue "Charité"-Staffel behandelt Cholera in Berlin 1831
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: ARD: New "Charité" season tackles cholera in Berlin 1831.
article.articleSummary: Cholera, caused by Vibrio cholerae, is a highly infectious diarrheal disease spread mainly through drinking water tainted with feces or vomit of patients and contaminated food. In severe cases, rapid loss of fluids and salts can cause death unless treated with prompt rehydration and electrolyte replacement. Historically, the 19th‑century Berlin outbreak (1831) followed the Ganges delta spread, fueling pandemics that killed millions; cholera remains a risk after disasters or conflicts when water systems fail. The ARD series Charité, supported by Berlin University Medical Center, returns for a fifth season, returning to history with a Berlin 1831 setting during the cholera outbreak. Hegel is noted as having died in that period. Filming occurred near Prague; streaming launches December 18, with TV airing around December 22. The plot centers on a young underassistant physician and colleagues confronting how to halt the disease.

triage.headline_ja: ARD:新「シャリテ」シーズンが1831年ベルリンのコレラを描く
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はテレビドラマ（フィクション）に関する内容であり、実際の感染症流行事例ではないため公衆衛生上のシグナルに該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事は1831年のベルリンにおけるコレラ流行を題材にしたテレビドラマ『Charité』の新シーズンに関する文化・エンタメ記事であり、現実の感染症発生事例ではない。対象国リストに該当する実際の発生国もない。

article.articleHeadline: 俄防鼠疫所女員工死因說法多變 中國網民恐慌質疑猜測(組圖)
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Divergent explanations for the death of a female employee at Russia's Plague Prevention Institute; Chinese netizens panic, question, and speculate (photo gallery).
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 8, 2026, divergent explanations surround the death of a laboratory technician at a Siberian plague research center in Irkutsk region. A 27-year-old female worker, who had traveled on assignment near the Mongolian border in Buryatia, died after an illness described by officials as unknown pneumonia; an alternative local report linked the death to exposure to plague. Nearly 200 people were quarantined in Irkutsk and surrounding areas amid concerns of a plague outbreak. Russia’s Rospotrebnadzor later said the death was due to an undetermined pneumonia and that tests found no microorganisms related to the worker’s duties. Independent outlets reported hospital quarantines and closures in the Baikal area, while government outlets deleted posts about possible plague. The incident follows heightened cross-border health drill activity: in August, China and Russia conducted a cross-border infectious-disease emergency drill in Fuyun, Heilongjiang, involving the Irkutsk institute. Chinese netizens reacted with fear and calls for transparency.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアのペスト予防研究所の女性職員の死因について見解が錯綜、中国のネットユーザーがパニックと疑念を表明（写真あり）
triage.triage_reason: ペスト研究機関職員の原因不明の死亡と約200人の隔離措置という異常事態があり、公式説明と現地報道が食い違う中で中国ネット上の社会的関心が高まっているため。
triage.notes: 事象の発生地はロシア（イルクーツク州・ブリヤート共和国）であり、対象国リストに含まれない。中国（黒竜江省富蘊）は8月の越境感染症訓練の実施場所として言及されているのみで、実際の発症・死亡事例は確認されていないため verified_locations には含めない。公式発表（原因不明の肺炎）と独立系報道（ペスト関連の可能性）が対立しており、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya Tightens Ebola Checks at Nairobi Airport on 7 October
article.articleSummary: Kenya tightened Ebola screening at Nairobi’s Jomo Kenyatta International Airport after confirming its first imported case on 6 October. Arrivals from 10 African countries—DRC, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Angola, Zambia, Tanzania and the Central African Republic—are now processed at Gate 16, with verified health details and disclosure of medicines taken in the prior month. The patient, a Kenyan citizen who had lived in the Democratic Republic of Congo, traveled via Uganda to Nairobi on Jambojet flight 8523 (3 October) and died at The Nairobi Hospital. Bundibugyo ebolavirus is involved; Congo’s outbreak had 8,665 confirmed cases and 4,178 deaths by 5 October. By 8 October, 57 contacts were identified (including 23 passengers and 4 crew), with 10 in quarantine. Kenya has 241 beds for isolation/treatment/quarantine, and WHO advises against travel restrictions. US travellers face unchanged entry rules; eTA and health-surveillance forms apply for eligible travelers.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、10月7日にナイロビ空港でのエボラ検疫を強化
triage.triage_reason: DRCで続くエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)大流行（8,665症例・4,178死亡）がケニアへの越境感染を引き起こし、国際的拡大とWHOの関与が確認されているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアでの空港検疫強化だが、実際の大規模アウトブレイクはDRCで発生しており、ケニアは輸入症例の発生国として言及されている。ザンビアなど他の対象国は検疫対象国リストに含まれるのみで、実際の症例発生国ではないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: 俄羅斯驚傳疑似鼠疫病例 已2死！WHO：尚未通報
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia reports a suspected plague case; two people have died already. WHO: not yet notified.
article.articleSummary: Russia reports a suspected plague-related death in Irkutsk Oblast: a first death from unknown pneumonia was reported Oct 2 at a plague prevention institute, and a second death on Oct 6 described as suspected plague. Russian authorities say no confirmed plague cases; an epidemiological investigation is under way, contacts have been traced and screened, and no high-threat pathogens detected so far. The WHO has not confirmed a plague case and continues risk assessment; the WHO Director-General urged Russia to clarify the exact cause of the initial pneumonia and the pathogen behind the public health measures, and to provide details on the second case. Globally (2019–2025), plague: 3,860 suspected, 2,646 confirmed, 423 deaths (~11% CFR); most confirmed in DRC and Madagascar; China 19 confirmed and Mongolia 17. Taiwan CDC says it is monitoring, enhances border fever screening, maintains laboratory capacity and antibiotics for treatment and post-exposure prophylaxis; no need to panic.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアで疑似ペスト症例が報告され、既に2人死亡！WHO：まだ通報なし
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツク州で原因不明肺炎後に疑似ペストによる死亡例が2件発生し、WHOがロシアに説明を要求するなど国際的関心が高まっており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際的拡大リスク）に該当するため。
triage.notes: 発生地域としてRussia、China、DRC、Madagascar、Mongoliaが記載されているが、記事の主題イベントはロシア・イルクーツク州での疑似ペスト死亡例であり、China・DRC・Madagascar・Mongoliaは2019-2025年の世界的なペスト統計の文脈で言及されているのみ。ロシアは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: 俄防鼠疫所女员工死因说法多变 中国网民恐慌质疑猜测(组图)
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cause of death explanations for a female employee at Russia's Plague Prevention Institute vary; Chinese netizens panic, question, and speculate (Photo Gallery).
article.articleSummary: A Siberian plague research center in Irkutsk region reported the death of a 27-year-old female laboratory technician, with the cause still unclear. Russian officials alternated between linking the death to plague and stating it was pneumonia of unknown etiology; tests reportedly found no pathogen related to her work. About 200 people near Irkutsk were quarantined due to suspected plague exposure. The case centers on a staffer who had traveled to the Buryatia region near the Mongolia border; one account says a container of dangerous pathogens was broken in the lab. The shifting official narratives prompted Chinese netizens to panic and speculate, recalling past outbreak scares and questioning transparency. BBC Chinese and other outlets reported inconsistencies and possible regional isolation, while a concurrent cross-border infectious-disease drill in FuYuan, Heilongjiang, underscored Sino-Russian concerns over cross-border disease control.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアのペスト防疫研究所の女性職員の死因、二転三転 中国ネット民はパニックと疑惑の声（写真特集）
triage.triage_reason: シベリアの研究施設で原因不明の死亡例が発生し、約200人が隔離されるなど異常性が高く、国境地帯での中露合同演習も行われるなど国際的な関心・越境リスクが示唆されるため。
triage.notes: 事件の発生地はロシア（イルクーツク州、ブリヤート共和国）であり、対象国リストには含まれない。中国（黒竜江省撫遠）での言及は越境防疫演習に関するものであり、実際の症例発生ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: State NVBDCP team reviews vector-borne disease control activities in Z'boto
article.articleSummary: Zunheboto district, Nagaland, Oct 5–7, 2026: A National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) team led by Dr Imnapokim and Deputy Director Dr Kavito Zhimomi conducted a three-day review of vector-borne disease prevention and control activities, with a sensitisation programme at DC Conference Hall on Oct 8. The review covered malaria trends 2018–2026 and dengue trends 2023–2026, and reviewed the district’s dengue and Japanese Encephalitis (JE) status. Participants from government departments, district authorities, churches and civil society discussed strengthening measures, including long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs), Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS), sanitation and environmental management, and school/church awareness, plus focal spraying. Deputy Commissioner Dharam Raj urged a coordinated, multi-sectoral approach, regular vector-control, timely diagnosis and treatment, and optimal use of resources. The State team highlighted District Task Force and District Elimination Committee roles and emphasised Testing, Treatment and Tracking (3Ts) for malaria elimination.

triage.headline_ja: 州NVBDCPチーム、ズンヘボト県で媒介感染症対策活動をレビュー
triage.triage_reason: これは既存の媒介感染症対策プログラムの定例レビュー会議に関する報告であり、新規の異常な感染拡大や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は2018-2026年のマラリアおよび2023-2026年のデング熱トレンドのレビュー会議についてであり、具体的な症例急増や異常事態の報告はない。通常の行政・プログラム活動報告のため見送りと判断。

article.articleHeadline: China extends $2 million support to Kenya for Ebola preparedness, drought relief
article.articleSummary: Kenya receives a $2 million (Ksh 260 million) grant from China to boost Ebola virus disease preparedness and drought relief. Of the total, $1 million funds Ebola preparedness, targeting counties identified as very high-risk and high-risk with enhanced surveillance, laboratory and diagnostic capacity, infection prevention and control, and health facilities equipped to detect and manage suspected Ebola cases. The remaining $1 million supports drought relief interventions. The funds were handed over in Nairobi by Chinese Ambassador Guo Haiyan to National Treasury Principal Secretary Chris Kiptoo, with Public Health Principal Secretary Mary Muthoni in attendance. The grant reinforces Kenya’s public health readiness and humanitarian response, aligned with Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) and the Global Development Initiative (GDI). Kenyan officials thanked China for prompt, development-focused assistance following Kenya’s request.

triage.headline_ja: 中国、ケニアのエボラ対策・干ばつ救援に200万ドルの支援を拡大
triage.triage_reason: 実際のエボラ発生事例ではなく、ケニアへのエボラ対策準備資金に関する援助ニュースであり、対象国での発生も確認されない。
triage.notes: 記事はケニアにおけるエボラ発生そのものではなく、準備態勢強化のための中国からの資金援助に関する内容。中国は資金提供国として言及されているのみで、発生国ではない。ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsは空配列。

article.articleHeadline: Proteína pouco conhecida é potencial alvo contra a doença de Chagas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A little-known protein is a potential target for Chagas disease.
article.articleSummary: IP6K protein in Trypanosoma cruzi identified as a promising target for Chagas disease by researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP) and collaborators. In laboratory tests, reducing IP6K production disrupts the parasite's infectious cycle in human cardiac cells, compromising differentiation into infectious bloodstream forms and diminishing replication across infection cycles. When both IP6K gene copies are deleted, parasites cannot survive to proceed with tests, underscoring IP6K's essential role, though the current study used parasites that still carried one copy. IP6K shows only about 25% sequence similarity to the human homolog, suggesting potential for selective drugs with fewer side effects. The findings, published in Communications Biology in August, position IP6K as a novel target for anti‑T. cruzi therapy—crucial for a neglected disease affecting millions worldwide. The work involves a two-host cycle with an insect vector (barbeiro/kissing bug) and mammalian hosts, including humans.

triage.headline_ja: シャーガス病に対する新たな治療標的として注目される未解明タンパク質
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は研究機関による基礎研究（創薬標的タンパク質の発見）に関する学術的報告であり、実際の疾病発生やアウトブレイクに関する情報ではないため、公衆衛生上の緊急対応は不要。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジル・サンパウロ大学の研究者によるシャーガス病治療薬開発に関する基礎科学研究の紹介であり、実際の感染事例やアウトブレイクの報告ではない。発生地域としてBrazilが付与されているが、疾病発生地点ではなく研究機関の所在地を示すものであるため、verified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Peste neumónica: qué tan peligrosa es, cómo se contagia y por qué la OMS pide tratarla de inmediato
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pneumonic plague: how dangerous it is, how it spreads, and why the WHO urges immediate treatment.
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague (Yersinia pestis) remains active globally, with wild rodent and flea reservoirs across Asia and the Americas; most human cases occur in Madagascar and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. A potential case in Siberia has reignited Russian surveillance, especially near the Russia–Mongolia border. In August 2026, scientists confirmed a major natural outbreak on the frontier, prompting a joint monitoring agreement through 2029 between the Irkutsk Institute for the Fight Against Plague in Siberia and the Far East. Pneumonic plague, the most dangerous form, spreads through airborne droplets and causes rapid deterioration: incubation of one to several days, then high fever, chills, fatigue, headache, chest pain, dyspnea, and bloody sputum; without timely treatment, death can occur within days. The WHO advises immediate antibiotics on suspicion, isolation, and prophylaxis for close contacts; with prompt care, recovery is likely, underscoring that the disease is dangerous but controllable.

triage.headline_ja: 肺ペスト：その危険性、感染経路、そしてWHOが即時治療を求める理由
triage.triage_reason: 記事はペスト菌全般の解説記事であり、主な焦点はロシア・モンゴル国境における動物由来の自然発生監視であって、対象国における具体的な新規発生イベントの報告ではない。
triage.notes: 記事はペスト菌（肺ペスト）の一般解説記事で、具体的な発生地はロシア（シベリア）とモンゴル国境地域。マダガスカル・DRCは既知の流行地域として言及されているのみで、今回の具体的イベントの発生国ではないため、対象国リストに該当する国はverified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Russia open to a Trump-Putin call as questions mount over plague lab death
article.articleSummary: Death at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute in Siberia: Darya Shipilova, 28, died on Oct 2 from pneumonia of unknown origin. Initial media reports tied the death to pneumonic plague after a lab accident, but Russia says no plague has been confirmed. The World Health Organization asked Russia’s Rospotrebnadzor for more information amid rumors of a second infection; Russia maintains no epidemic risk. About 200 people were quarantined or monitored; nearly 5,000 tests found no dangerous pathogens, and 90% of those under monitoring were released. Shipilova had vaccination against the pathogens she worked with, implying immunity. The Irkutsk lab conducts countermeasure research and bioterrorism preparedness; reports note cooperation with Chinese authorities and a cross-border outbreak drill. Moscow is open to a prompt Trump–Putin call to discuss the death, though no date has been set; U.S. agencies monitor about 200 travelers annually from the region.

triage.headline_ja: ペスト研究所での死亡事件を巡る疑問が高まる中、ロシアはトランプ・プーチン電話会談に前向き
triage.triage_reason: シベリアの抗ペスト研究所職員の原因不明の肺炎による死亡事件で、WHOがロシア当局に追加情報を要請するなど国際的な関心・懸念が高まっており、IHR基準（異常性・国際的拡大リスク）が2つ該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: イベントはロシア（シベリア・イルクーツク州）で発生しており、対象国リストに該当する国なし。中国は協力関係・訓練の文脈で言及されているのみで発生地ではないため除外。ロシア当局はペスト確定を否定しているが、WHOが情報提供を求めるなど国際的な注目度は高い。

article.articleHeadline: En RDC, "le manque de coopération complique la riposte contre Ébola"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the DRC, "the lack of cooperation complicates the Ebola response."
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 4,018 deaths and 8,300 confirmed cases as of October 2, with the outbreak first detected in May in Ituri and spreading to seven northern and eastern provinces, including North Kivu (Goma). MSF warns of worsening transmission in the region. Catholic Bishop Willy Ngumbi of Goma warns that lack of cooperation and distrust in information hinder the response, even as the Church, health services, and civil society intensify sensitization efforts in areas like Butembo-Beni.
